David Raya and Jurrien Timber deals show Arsenal are serious about protecting their title-winning core

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal are continuing their excellent work in retaining their key players as David Raya and Jurrien Timber have both been approached about upcoming contracts.
  • Industry observers note that this comes after Declan Rice signed a five-year contract extension.
  • Industry observers note that timber has reportedly agreed better terms, and Raya is also on the verge of a fresh deal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal are continuing their excellent work in retaining their key players as David Raya and Jurrien Timber have both been approached about upcoming contracts.

Industry observers note that this comes after Declan Rice signed a five-year contract extension. The midfielder will now stay at the Emirates until 2031, but Mikel Arteta is now close to locking down more defenders in his squad.

Industry observers note that timber has reportedly agreed better terms, and Raya is also on the verge of a fresh deal. Although both deals are yet to be officially announced, it shows how important Arsenal are trying to keep them at the top.

The importance of retaining Raya and Timber is evident.

In a recent development, since arriving at the club from Brentford, Raya has become Arteta’s first choice in goal. He has become an notable part of Arsenal’s attacking play due to his distribution, decision-making and game under pressure.

His performances have also earned him honours outside of North London as he was named in the 2026 FIFPRO World 11. Only the second Arsenal player to win the award after Thierry Henry in 2006.

Raya has a contract in place until 2028, although he was given better financial terms last year. However, a new long-term deal will offer more security to one of Arteta’s most trusted players.

Since joining from Ajax in 2023, Timber has become a key part of Arsenal’s backline. Despite injury concerns, he has proven to be one of the most dependable defenders in the squad.

He can play as a right back, left back and centre back which provides Arteta with great versatility. He has the physicality and technical ability to help Arsenal at both ends of the pitch.

According to recent reports, it has been reported that Timber has agreed to better terms. How long his contract is for is unknown.

There is a pattern beginning to emerge from Arsenal’s recent contract news.

It has been revealed that rice has been signed until 2031. Timber is also expected to sign, committing his peak years to the club. Raya is also expected to sign soon, with talks said to be at an advanced stage.

Arteta recently signed a contract extension until 2030. They aren’t just trying to keep their best players for another year but are looking to create consistency within the squad and management.

This is an issue for any club competing within the domestic and European leagues, as it can cause problems with team cohesion and development due to constant change of key players.

While there is still work to be done, this is positive news for fans.

Signing Raya and Timber will ensure that two key components of Arteta’s backline are safe. It will also show that with Rice’s newly introduced contract, they’re looking to build on their recent success and not let their best players near the end of their contracts.

Funny ha-ha or funny peculiar? Yesterday had plenty of both

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1771 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Here’s a question: did last night’s Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2 match at St James’ Park show we can be the equal of the reigning Premier League champions?
  • At 16 minutes past six, after a miserably one-sided first half, you would have been embarking on mission impossible to find anyone saying “yes” among the 52,000+plus in the stadium or the millions watching on TV.
  • By the final whistle, blown nearly 10 minutes after the 90 by Chris Kavanagh, few would have replied “no”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Here’s a question: did last night’s Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2 match at St James’ Park show we can be the equal of the reigning Premier League champions?

At 16 minutes past six, after a miserably one-sided first half, you would have been embarking on mission impossible to find anyone saying “yes” among the 52,000+plus in the stadium or the millions watching on TV.

By the final whistle, blown nearly 10 minutes after the 90 by Chris Kavanagh, few would have replied “no”. Such is football.

Industry observers note that let’s start at the beginning, or at least on the 12.30 Azuma train from King’s Cross to Newcastle. The LNER service was predictably packed with Gooners. Passengers in Carriage J were overwhelming confident of a one-nil or two-nil to the Arsenal, as they like to crow in north London.

Recent findings suggest that based on their team’s results this season, that was to be expected. They don’t score many and, apart from a blip near Brighton, they concede even fewer.

Industry observers note that arsenal are, in a word, efficient. I find them boring. The descriptions are not mutually exclusive. No way as the train rumbled into the magnificent Central Station about 32 minutes late was I looking forward to a feast of entertaining football.

Sources indicate that in dire need of a drink, I walked up Pink Lane with Big Nige, who had boarded the delayed train at York after it made an unscheduled stop south of the old Viking stronghold of Jorvik. Known as Eboracum in Roman times, btw.

Pink Lane was awash with happy Londoners. There are many, many reasons to be proud of Newcastle; one is the warm welcome the natives offer strangers (excluding Mackems, obviously. There have to be limits).

Which was why the mild hostility that greeted me in the Mosaic Tap was a big surprise. A young chap called Rob walked up to our table, where Paul and Gowa had already got in the drinks, and noted: “You can’t wear that scarf in here.”.

His mate had apparently clocked me as a Gooner, having mistaken my half-and-half for an Arsenal favour.

Recent findings suggest that A little bit of background. Remarked scarf was a souvenir from the Bayer Leverkusen v NUFC match. Not that I bought it on my visit to the BayArena shop a mere 11 months ago, when it would have cost £20. This one was acquired in October for a tenner in the NUFC pre-Christmas online sale, while present-buying for my daughter Jo and her family. The PIF need all the help they can get . . .

Industry observers note that for all those who detest a half-and-half, that’s your prerogative. I view it as a reminder of a great trip, more useful than a match programme and less likely to be lost.

In a recent development, rob swiftly realised his error, probably because I had slipped into my best am dram persona by screaming: “Look at the scarf! Look at it! You need to go to Specsavers, mate!”.

Industry observers note that the faux outrage reduced poor Rob to a gibbering, hilariously apologetic wreck. “Sorry, sorry, I’m really sorry. It was my mate . . . What are you drinking, can I get you one, please?”.

The free glass of malbec was much appreciated, thanks. Considering the prices at Mosaic, the scarf has probably paid for itself. Funny ha-ha, Rob.

According to recent reports, we played the “who would you select” game and all four of us agreed Gonzalez was not justifying his place. Starting Steur was a no-brainer, the back five picked themselves, based on the Fulham game, with Livramento available if needed to give us a second-half lift. The midfield and attack, apart from Steur and Barnes, were as clear as a peasouper.

The major news at 4.15 was Bruno G starting for his latest team. Who had expected that?

Recent findings suggest that there was just time for a quick one in Bar Loco, where I bumped into the legendary Tony Mallabar, before safely negotiating Turnstile 31 at the Leazes End. My seat in row MM was in line with the edge of the six-yard box, which gave a perfect view of the fourth goal, unfortunately.

Industry observers note that the Booing of Bruno had been a hot topic. My opinion is that every opposition player should be relentlessly jeered, booed, abused and barracked (isn’t SJP on Barrack Road for a reason?) That’s what I recall, perhaps falsely, from big games in the Seventies . . .

Sources indicate that anyway, the Brazilian midfielder was booed from the warm-up until his replacement by Lewis-Skelly when we were leading 2-1. The effort of singling out our former captain probably backfired, because it distracted the more vocal supporters from doing the job of cheering their favourites.

Not that the players or the play gave reasons to be buoyant in the first half. Arsenal did what Arsenal do, using their 11 players against our outfield 10. Whenever Osula or Willock or Murphy or Barnes or Steur attempted to put pressure on Raya, he found the spare man whom our would-be presser had just left unmarked. Boring and efficient by Arsenal. Half-cocked and aimless by the Mags.

Recent findings suggest that in my opinion, Arsenal are no great shakes, whatever the title claims. A great team have a top, top striker. They don’t. As they proved by managing only one effort on target before the interval. Hornicek didn’t have a prayer once Hall chested down a long ball and instantly lost possession near the edge of his box.

Our left-back is a wonderful footballer but, having rarely played as a defender in his youth at Chelsea, he is still learning some of the skills essential to be a watertight obstacle.

Industry observers note that murphy tried to catch Raya off his line with a speculative long-range effort and one other shot flew narrowly wide of Raya’s left post via a deflection off Barnes. There was almost nothing else of note in the first half as the champions biffed nearly every shot high, wide and ugly.

Recent findings suggest that burn and Thiaw stood reasonably firm, Dedic and Murphy seemed on different wavelengths, Steur harried Bruno G and Barnes demonstrated some unlikely aggression. Miley plugged away and Osula ran gamely but United lacked any sort of perceptible gameplan. We rarely managed to find a player in space. Worrying times.

In a recent development, where was our next goal coming from, wondered my mate Dave at the interval. It had been a while at SJP.

In a recent development, the answer came within four minutes of the restart, soon after the first of three stoppages caused by apparent injuries to Raya. More importantly, after Matthias Jaissle made a triple substitution.

It has been revealed that harvey Barnes smashed a shot low to the keeper’s right, ending a quick attack. Willock had pressured Odegaard into presenting the ball to Osula. An assist on the headless chicken’s credits, fitting reward for another tireless display.

Recent findings suggest that this was when the match became funny peculiar. Miley man-marked Bruno, Arsenal misplaced passes, United won 50:50s, we found space to run with purpose. The gulf in monetary and player resources vanished as the Mags reverted to our best version of Howe-ball.

Only Hornicek of the summer 2026 signings was still on the pitch, Steur having been subbed.

Sources indicate that arsenal looked distinctly second-best. Raya went down again. A corner on our right from Hall was aimed beyond the far post, where the unstoppable Man from Blyth powered a header goalwards. In a frantic kerfuffle, a couple of blocks merely delayed the inevitable. Thiaw smashed it home and we were ahead.

Funny ha-ha and funny peculiar.

It has been revealed that around me in row MM, the earlier, almost incessant moans and grounds became voices of encouragement. Supporters who had failed to back their team in a dire first half were suddenly full of the joys of November . . .

Ramsey, Livramento and Elanga all caused Arsenal problems. For a few minutes, we battered them.

According to recent reports, then Raya collapsed for a third time. The long delay gave the champions a break they desperately needed.

Whatever anyone else states, Jaissle and his men were right to keep pressing for a third. Arsenal were always going to fashion at least one good chance in the time remaining after we went ahead. To sit back with 28 minutes left, plus a lot of stoppage time, would have been professional suicide.

Industry observers note that my suspicion is that those who now bemoan our aggressive play would have whinged even more if the team had sat back. The match became attack and counter-attack. Arsenal, through Madueke doing a decent impression of the absent Saka, kept cutting onto his left foot. Hall, sometimes having to mark two opponents, let the right winger swerve inside and slam a low shot through two defenders and past Hornicek.

The keeper got two hands to the ball but could only push it into the Leazes End net.

Havertz nearly produced what would have been a truly wonderful moment when his head diverted a late Hall corner beyond Kepa and against the crossbar. So near, yet so far.

Then Barnes capped what I reckon was his best game since Wembley 2025 by outstripping Rice on the left touchline and playing the ball perfectly to Ramsey on the edge of the 18-yard box.

Sources indicate that in the words of John Ando Anderson, just hit the bloody thing, man. Ramsey did. Sadly, though, instead of putting his laces through it, he tried to bend the ball into the postage stamp and it flew high and wide.

Industry observers note that what a feather in Jaissle’s cap a win would have been. One point was good, three would have been great.

In a recent development, the late introduction of Wissa, who replaced Willock, was a failure. He contributed almost nothing, which has been the story all too often since his expensive arrival.

Recent findings suggest that I would have thrown on Fernandez-Pardo as the game opened up. No team enjoy speedy opponents running hard at them and the Belgium international could have been the joker in Jaissle’s pack.

On the balance of play a draw was reasonable but this, like the Liverpool result, felt like two points dropped.

What is inarguable is the team’s willingness to battle for their mates, their manager and the Toon. Long may that continue.

Arsenal mourns Peter Storey: 1971 Double-winning hero dies aged 81

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal have expressed their condolences in the passing of former player Peter Storey.
  • It has been revealed that storey was an influential member of one of the most successful sides in the club’s history.
  • Storey was a key figure in the famous run as he helped keep the FA Cup hopes alive with a display against Stoke City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal have expressed their condolences in the passing of former player Peter Storey.

It has been revealed that storey was an influential member of one of the most successful sides in the club’s history. The midfielder appeared in 501 games for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, winning the First Division and FA Cup during the 1970/71 season.

Storey was a key figure in the famous run as he helped keep the FA Cup hopes alive with a display against Stoke City.

Industry observers note that A statement from the club confirmed his death on Tuesday (17th November). The club will pay tribute to Storey in their Champions League tie against Borussia Dortmund on 24th November.

Storey signed as an apprentice with Arsenal in 1961, and made his first-team debut in October 1965 in a game against Leicester City.

In a recent development, he was later converted to a central midfielder by manager Bertie Mee and coach Don Howe. Storey became an invaluable member of the squad due to his aggressive play, work-rate and versatility.

In 1970 Storey was part of the side that won the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, and the following year Arsenal won the league and FA Cup double.

Storey played a key role in an amazing FA Cup semi-final in April 1971. After Arsenal had looked like they were losing, Storey scored a last-minute penalty to make it 2-2.

Arsenal won the replay to get to the final, beating Liverpool to win their first-ever double.

It has been revealed that storey scored 17 goals in 501 games for Arsenal. This puts him in joint 8th place in the most appearances for the club.

Storey enjoyed success at club level and earned his first cap for England in 1971. He earned a total of 19 caps for England.

Industry observers note that he played for England until 1973. In 1977, Storey left Arsenal to join Fulham, meaning he had a 12-year stint at the north London club.

He played 19 games for Fulham before retiring from professional football in 1978.

Following his football career, Storey had a difficult time. He was imprisoned for a number of crimes. In 2010, he wrote an autobiography, True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man, detailing these events in his life.

He will be remembered in Arsenal history for his impressive contribution to the club. Having made 501 appearances for the club, he was a key member of the squad that won the Double in 1971.

Playing against Borussia Dortmund will be a great way for fans to pay tribute to one of the key players in a special time in the history of the club.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The first 11 games of the Serie A season have produced some rather intriguing trends regarding AC Milan’s attacking productivity.
  • MilanNews recall how – after the vital win in Genoa before the break – Ruben Amorim emphasised how this Milan team are still far from the final product he envisioned in the summer, especially in the final third.
  • The Rossoneri are improving in possession control and chance creation, but they often remain too far from the opponent’s penalty area for most of the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The first 11 games of the Serie A season have produced some rather intriguing trends regarding AC Milan’s attacking productivity.

MilanNews recall how – after the vital win in Genoa before the break – Ruben Amorim emphasised how this Milan team are still far from the final product he envisioned in the summer, especially in the final third.

The Rossoneri are improving in possession control and chance creation, but they often remain too far from the opponent’s penalty area for most of the game. This limitation has also affected Gonçalo Ramos, who has been forced to drop deeper, far away from the penalty box.

After 11 league games, Milan are only 17th in Serie A for shots on goal, averaging 11.5 per game. Yet, they lead Serie A in average xG per shot, at 0.145. In other words, the Rossoneri do not shoot much, but when they do it is very dangerous.

Industry observers note that this is also confirmed by the remarkable individual numbers. Adrien Rabiot has scored five goals from 12 shots, with a conversion rate of 41.7%. Diego Moreira is at 40%, Alphadjo Cisse at 38.5%, and Christian Pulisic at 36.4%.

The notable absentee from this ranking is the player expected to score the most: Gonçalo Ramos. The Portuguese has scored just three goals with 33 total shots and 5.35 xG, meaning a conversion rate of 9.1%. These numbers are far from those of his team-mates.

Amorim continues to defend him, emphasising that the problem lies primarily with the team being too deep. Milan must therefore start to generate more territorial dominance, to allow Ramos to operate closer to goal and for him to be on the end of what is clearly quality service being provided.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal head to St James’ Park this Saturday for their first match after the international break. They could be faced with a weakened Newcastle midfield.

Industry observers note that joelinton missed training before the international break because of a thigh injury that also kept him out of the 1-1 draw with Fulham. Now, he needs to have an MRI scan to check the seriousness of his injury.

It has been revealed that this is a huge blow for Jaissle. Joelinton’s physicality and intensity will be very difficult to find in another player, especially when the Gunners put pressure on Newcastle.

Sources indicate that it may help Mikel Arteta’s team to dominate in midfield. They must ensure that they match the level of physicality of Newcastle and adjust with the away game itself. Joelinton’s absence may require Newcastle to make some changes in their style of play from midfield.

Industry observers note that joelinton has struggled to make an impact in the Premier League this season. He’s played only three games, and is now set to be sidelined again.

Recent findings suggest that however, it has been suggested that Joelinton could return before Christmas. Further medical tests must be performed to determine the exact amount of time that he will be out for.

Joelinton is a concern. He is very physical and can regain the ball effectively in midfield. He can also help Newcastle move the ball forward.

Sources indicate that if Newcastle are unable to match that intensity, it could allow Arsenal to dominate the game. Declan Rice and Bruno Guimarães are both in good form, meaning that the Gunners have a solid foundation in order to succeed, and stop the hosts from taking control.

Willock and Gonzalez have both been absent due to illness, but they should be fit to play on Saturday.

According to recent reports, jaissle has more options to consider with Joelinton missing. Jacob Ramsey is also now available after serving his suspension.

Newcastle have some good news regarding Matias Fernandez-Pardo. The £51 million signing has been suffering from a long-term virus and was unable to play in Belgium’s last internationals. However, he appears to be improving.

Recent findings suggest that he has returned to training so could make the starting XI after coming on as a substitute in the game against Fulham. Since moving to the club from France, he has played 6 games in the Premier League.

Despite Joelinton being absent, Newcastle will still be a dangerous opponent. A calm performance from Arsenal will be required in order to take 3 points from the match.

With Joelinton missing, Arsenal can assert control in midfield. As they look to stay on top of the league table, exploiting the injury complications in Newcastle’s team should be a priority.

Nick Woltemade was left out of the Juventus starting eleven on Sunday.

A Serie A home match against Venezia.

After a woeful goalless opening half Juventus were booed off the pitch.

Nick Woltemade introduced for the start of the second half and the rest is history.

Within 14 minutes Juventus had the game won.

Nick Woltemade scoring the opening goal within eight minutes of entering the pitch.

It was then 2-0 within 14 minutes as the Newcastle United loan star got the assist for Teun Koopmeiners.

Juan Cabal a third goal, before then Nick Woltemade passed up the chance of scoring his second when he handed the ball to fellow striker Randal Kolo Muani to score from the penalty spot.

A goalless first half shocker transformed into a thumping second half 4-0 Juventus triumph.

Supersub Nick Woltemade handed the man of the match trophy after the final whistle.

In a recent development, when Sports Dunia reported on the match. they waxed lyrical about the contribution of Nick Woltemade: ‘Came on and instantly changed the game. His close-range finish for the opener broke Venezia’s resistance and shifted all momentum. We noticed his intelligent movement between lines, dragging defenders out of shape. He also assisted Koopmeiners, showing composure in the box. From our perspective, a superb super-sub performance.’.

Nick Woltemade has still only started seven games in all competitions for Juventus but now has eight direct goal contributions, scoring five and getting three assists.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that in the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Overpowered and overrun, Arsenal were subjected to the sort of gruelling treatment they usually inflict on their opponents. Mikel Arteta’s side did not look anything like Premier League champions here, as Brighton and Hove Albion produced a stunning performance full of swarming energy and breathless bravery.

Sources indicate that in the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns. This sort of thing simply does not happen to Arteta’s side. Well, it did not happen. Not before this monstering on the south coast, where the Brighton fans were whipped into a frenzy by the brilliance of Fabian Hürzeler’s players.

It has been revealed that brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field. They even scored with a set-piece, as one of Arsenal’s great strengths became a sudden weakness. Everywhere Arteta looked, the foundational truths of his team were being shaken by a Brighton storm. It was their first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023, also against Brighton.

Remarkably, this is now the third consecutive season in which Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions. They are rarely happier than when they are on the hunt against more illustrious opponents, working as a team to snap at heels and then attacking in numbers. They are known as the Seagulls, but they played more like a pack of bloodthirsty wolves. The ferocity of their off-the-ball work, especially in the first half, was extraordinary.

Not for a long time have Arsenal been as rattled as they were here. David Raya misplaced passes, Gabriel Magalhães lost duels and Bruno Guimarães chased the ball in vain. It was Brighton’s Pascal Gross, rather than Arsenal’s Martin Odegaard, who shaped the game in midfield. It was Brighton’s Charalampos Kostoulas, rather than Arsenal’s Kai Havertz, who offered incisive class in attack.

It has been revealed that gross and Kostoulas both struck from range in a one-sided first half, before Chema Andrés added the third after the break. At half-time, Arteta had sprinted down the tunnel towards the dressing room. Whatever messages he gave to his players, they either did not sink in or did not work. By the end, Arsenal were lucky the scoreline was not even more humiliating.

Sources indicate that arteta’s players had come through some tricky assignments in winning their first seven matches of this season, but this was their toughest test yet and they failed it badly. They did not handle the emotions of the occasion particularly well, either: in stoppage time, a frustrated Declan Rice kicked out at Malick Yalcouyé. He was perhaps fortunate to avoid a red card.

It has been revealed that it was the first time that Rice and Guimarães had started alongside each other for Arsenal and it quickly became clear that their £180m partnership will need some work. Arsenal would have hoped their experience in the Premier League would allow for an instant connection but, evidently, that is not the case. Guimarães was hooked after 60 minutes, but might easily have been removed at the break.

In a recent development, both managers had a similar assessment of the match and how it was won: Brighton did the basics far better than Arsenal. “How we wanted to approach this game was getting into it through small wins,” Hürzeler said. “Everyone speaks about a goal or chance as a win, but a small win can be the first throw-in, the first corner, win the first header, win the first tackle. These small things. If you win these small steps, and celebrate them as a win, then you can gain bigger and bigger wins.”.

It was typical of Brighton that one of their fresh signings produced an excellent performance in midfield. Andrés, a 21-year-old Spaniard signed from Stuttgart at the end of the transfer window, looks to be the latest gem identified by their data-led recruitment model. No one inside the Amex Stadium was thinking about Carlos Baleba, sold to Manchester United, when Andrés made his tackles and won his headers.

Another upcoming signing, centre-back Luka Vuskovic, was similarly impressive at the back. Signed for £46m from Tottenham Hotspur, Vuskovic looks more than capable of going to the top of the game.

In a recent development, this was perhaps the first occasion this season in which Arsenal missed William Saliba, the injured centre-back who has been so fundamental to their success in recent years. The Frenchman can always be relied on to provide calmness and composure at the back, even under intense pressure. Without him, Arsenal were uncharacteristically jittery.

“The amount of technical errors we did in our own half...” Arteta bemoaned. “We didn’t respect any principle of play that you have to get out of those man-to-man situations. That put us always on the back foot.”.

Sources indicate that gross, who at 35 is playing as well as ever, opened the scoring with a low shot from range after 31 minutes. Kostoulas then struck the second, from a similar distance, after some end-to-end action resulted in Arsenal’s midfield and defence melting away. The third was the most simple, as Andrés headed in at the back post from an inswinging corner.

According to recent reports, arsenal did have some chances, with Havertz missing the best of them, but there was never a sense that Brighton were vulnerable. The pressure on the home side was never sustained. For Arteta, who now has an extended international break in which to ruminate on this defeat, it all made for an unfamiliar and unexpected pain.

Mikel Arteta stated his Arsenal players failed to “respect the game” as their perfect start to the season was ended in stunning style by a brilliant Brighton performance.

Arsenal’s capitulation on the south coast led to their first defeat of the campaign and Arteta admitted that Brighton had a different “edge” and “bite” throughout the match. The Arsenal manager also said the 3-0 loss represented a “major lesson” for his players.

Sources indicate that “There are certain basics you need to accomplish in football, especially in the Premier League, that we were very far from,” Arteta stated. “From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear.

Sources indicate that “It was a really disappointing result and performance. Brighton were another gear up from us. We were extremely poor technically and were not respecting the game.

“It is not going to take away what the team has done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup. What we have done and the way we have competed, and the amount of games we have won, has been remarkable. But this is a massive lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level.”.

Arteta added that his team did not “respect the principles of play” that were required against Brighton’s intense pressing, and also said his players were guilty of numerous technical errors.

“Credit to Brighton for what they have done because they have overcome us and they had another edge,” Arteta remarked. “There are a lot of moments when the ball is 50/50 and it changes hands and most of the time it was for them.”.

Brighton are the Premier League’s top scorers this season with 16 goals in five matches so far, and this emphatic victory took them up to third place in the table.

“It was a special win,” Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton head coach, remarked. “Not only because we played the best team in England but because of the performance. I am really proud of my team. It’s always crucial to enjoy these moments. We were horrible to play against. My players really trust each other on the pitch.”.

Two things, one give credit to them. In the manner that they played and committed to every single action. We were below the standards that are required for us but in the Premier League as well.

Sources indicate that when you miss chances like we did it becomes impossible. I want to congratulate Brighton for what they’ve done. It’s a significant lesson for us to learn. Mikel Arteta has clamped down on Arsenal stars' Fantasy Premier League (FPL) exploits after 'Tzatziki FC', Christos Tzolis' team, 'leaked' team news.

The Arsenal manager admitted he has 'taken measures' to ensure opponents are not given an advantage by his players' selections on the popular game.

Tzolis picked himself as captain of his FPL side prior to the Gunners' 1-0 victory over Liverpool, a clear indication that he would start after recently coming back from injury.

Arteta then caught wind of the situation and Tzolis removed all Arsenal players from his fantasy team for their next game against Hull.

X account FPL Focal identified 'Tzatziki FC' as the Greek winger's team and screenshots of his teams from both game weeks indicated how his picks changed.

On Friday, speaking about this issue, Arteta said: 'With Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well. Constantly they are asking me about line-ups as well, because they want to know.

Christos Tzolis picked himself in Fantasy Premier League before starting the Liverpool game.

Tzolis' team, seen here before the Liverpool clash, is called 'Tzatziki FC' and was identified as his side by X account FPL Focal.

Industry observers note that 'It’s a topic, you know. These are the kind of things that are happening in our society right now and it’s something latest.

Recent findings suggest that 'We haven’t dealt with it [before] and we need to put latest things in place. Obviously confidentiality is something critical because it’s about trust and about what you are trying to do and that should be kept as a huge secret. We’ll take measures to make sure it doesn’t happen.'.

Arteta then confirmed that those measures had already been taken.

Tzolis is a known obsessive of the game, which puts him among 13 million other players who participate every year.

He even quipped after providing an assist against Coventry earlier in the season: 'I will take the three points', referring to the FPL score for doing so.

Chelsea had a similar issue this season, with their players indicating that Joao Pedro was out injured, removing the Brazilian from their FPL teams before his absence was confirmed by the club.

Teams are taking the matter seriously and are keen to ensure any possible advantage their opponents might have regarding team news is nipped in the bud.

Five years ago, Aston Villa stopped their players from participating in FPL after a number of them took Jack Grealish out of their line-ups, notifying eagle-eyed competitors that he was injured.

Mikel Arteta has cracked down on FPL use and 'taken measures' to ensure there are no leaks.

The potential impact of players joining the global GTA 6 mania is another concern for Arteta, with a number of top-flight players already sharing how gripped they will be by the new game.

Bryan Mbeumo posted the loading screen at midnight on Thursday, indicating that he was having a late-night gaming session just days before the Liverpool clash, while Alexander Isak has remarked he will be hunkering down to play the game.

Declan Rice has previously spoken about how he often games into the early hours after matches when adrenaline is still coursing through him.

And his manager noted: 'We’ll try to find out how much exposure we have to these kinds of games and make sure it’s the right one to be able to perform and focus on what we have to do.'.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Reworded scientific phrases can thwart publishers’ plagiarism checkers, but, in many cases, the resulting combinations of words only draw more attention from scientific sleuths.
  • These days, I spend a lot of my time looking through published papers that I suspect are fraudulent.
  • According to recent reports, I retired in 2022 from the University of Oxford, UK, where I worked as a developmental neuropsychologist.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Reworded scientific phrases can thwart publishers’ plagiarism checkers, but, in many cases, the resulting combinations of words only draw more attention from scientific sleuths. Credit: Gregory Dubus/iStock via Getty.

These days, I spend a lot of my time looking through published papers that I suspect are fraudulent. It is a gruelling task. But amid the tedium, there is some light relief, thanks to some hilarious phrases used by authors seeking to avoid detection by plagiarism checkers. It’s hard not to smile when ‘breast cancer’ becomes ‘bosom peril’, or a citation for ‘Baker and Logue’ become ‘Pastry Specialist and Logue’.

According to recent reports, I retired in 2022 from the University of Oxford, UK, where I worked as a developmental neuropsychologist. I now track down research fraud as part of a community of scientific sleuths. We work together to identify papers that we consider to be problematic in some way, then send the evidence to publishers or post it on PubPeer, a post-publication peer-review platform. Our aim is for the problematic papers to be investigated and, if appropriate, retracted by their publishers. But, often, publishers are slower and more recalcitrant than many sleuths would like them to be.

‘A waste of time for all of us’: caught in the crossfire of the peer-review wars.

‘A waste of time for all of us’: caught in the crossfire of the peer-review wars.

It has been revealed that many people blame academia’s ‘publish or perish’ research culture for the rise in problematic papers. Without a large number of publications and citations, prospects for employment, promotion and glittering prizes evaporate. Some researchers cut corners, manipulate or fabricate data, or copy the work of other scientists without citing them.

The demand for desperate researchers to get their name on a publication in any journal has spawned semi-professional organizations known as paper mills. These sell authorship status, with prices that vary depending on the impact factor of the journal. Articles are typically generated using artificial-intelligence tools or plagiarized, and tend to find homes in journals that lack sufficient editorial scrutiny.

One of the few amusing consequences of these developments is the phenomenon of tortured phrases, first described in 2021 by computer scientists Guillaume Cabanac and Cyril Labbé and software engineer Alexander Magazinov1. They analysed huge volumes of research literature to identify patterns. Tortured phrases arise when someone — or, in most cases, a computer — replaces words in a published article with synonyms to evade plagiarism detectors and ultimately publish the result as their own work.

Authorship for sale: Nature investigates how paper mills work.

Authorship for sale: Nature investigates how paper mills work.

Cabanac and colleagues developed a free website called the Problematic Paper Screener, which documents tortured phrases and other red flags in publications. Detection of tortured phrases has been a communal effort by research sleuths, who document specific articles with tortured phrases on PubPeer.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03040-z.

Tech Report: Newcastle United Game Management problem is huge Red Herring

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (685 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The glitch of Newcastle United Game Management has reared its head once again.
  • It always hurts when you take the lead and end up drawing, or even worse, lose.
  • After the 2-2 draw with Arsenal, I have heard and read a fair few fans questioning the Newcastle United Game Management.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The glitch of Newcastle United Game Management has reared its head once again.

It always hurts when you take the lead and end up drawing, or even worse, lose.

Especially if it is a late goal that is conceded.

After the 2-2 draw with Arsenal, I have heard and read a fair few fans questioning the Newcastle United Game Management.

What these fans are questioning, is basically whyafter coming back to lead against Arsenal with 62 minutes on the clock, why couldn’t Matthias Jaissle and his players see out the rest of the match without conceding?

The 3 positives and 3 negatives piece on The Mag this Monday morning perfectly summed up the kind of thing I have been seeing.

David Punton selecting ‘Game Management’ as one of his three negatives and saying: ‘Another winning position has been thrown away. The same thing happened down at Fulham. It drives you crackers at times. They surely must have to work on how to see a game out? It’s not rocket science.’.

So is this true, the Newcastle United Game Management a huge concern?

Or is it a major fat Red Herring?

First of all I have had a look at the 14 Newcastle United matches this season from purely a statistical viewpoint.

Do Newcastle United repeatedly take the lead and throw it away?

Newcastle United when scoring the opening goal of the game this season, what ended up the final result? Won 4 (Spurs, Millwall, Hull, Palace), Drawn 2 (Liverpool, Fulham) Lost 0.

Newcastle United when conceding the opening goal of the game this season, what ended up the final result? Won 1 (West Brom), Drawn 2 (Bournemouth, Arsenal) Lost 5 (Leeds, Coventry, Villa, Everton x2).

Which matches have Newcastle United scored the final goal of the game? Happened seven times (West Brom, Spurs, Bournemouth, Millwall, Leeds, Palace, Everton cup).

Which matches have Newcastle United conceded the final goal of the game? Happened seven times (Liverpool, Hull, Coventry, Villa, Everton, Fulham, Arsenal).

In his Positives and Negatives piece, David Punton says about the supposed failings of Newcastle United Game Management: ‘They surely must have to work on how to see a game out? It’s not rocket science.’.

I am not just having a go at David here but what exactly is this magical way of ensuring that there is zero chance of allowing the opposition to score once you have taken the lead?

Newcastle United went 2-1 up on 62 minutes, so Arsenal had what turned out to be 37 minutes to get an equaliser (and then potential winner…).

They are the best team in the Premier League and have the strongest bench.

What is the absolute certain route to not letting them score?

As the stats show above, Newcastle United have given as good as they have got this season when it comes to scoring first and the eventual result, compared to the games when the opposition have scored first.

If you are leading by a single goal and it is the last minute of a match, then all your defenders recklessly charge up the pitch and you concede, that would be really poor Newcastle United Game Management.

It would be really poor Newcastle United Game Management if leading and then gifted an equaliser when trying a daft risky pass on the edge of your own penalty area.

This didn’t happen on Saturday, nor indeed at Fulham in the previous match.

Arsenal scored with 21 minutes left to play when some excellent play got them up the pitch and Madueke scored a good goal, which even though it went through a Newcastle defender’s legs you think Lukas Hornicek should have saved it.

Newcastle scored in the 80th minute at Craven Cottage and Fulham had to throw everything at them, they got the benefit of a bit of a scramble in our penalty area and two deflections contributed to their equaliser.

This isn’t disastrous Newcastle United Game Management, this is football.

It is a huge Red Herring to claim this is a serious problem this season for Matthias Jaissle and his team.

In a recent development, A year ago, the conditions weren’t there, but now they might be. Van Dijk’s contract expires in June and he’s always been fascinated by Milan and Italy. It’s complex, but it’s worth a try, and Cardinale seems to agree.

Then there is Gabriele Calvani. He’s Italian, 22, plays for Frosinone, and is expected to start San Siro on Sunday. The Diavolo are interested, just as they are keen on Sporting CP’s Gonçalo Inacio, whom Amorim has already coached and attempted to sign in the summer.

Milan will undoubtedly make some changes to their bench over the next 12 months, aiming to mix young players with experienced players. Filippo Terracciano will leave in January, Vladimirov needs to play, Hutchinson is on loan until June, and Jashari will have to reconsider his future.

It’s certain that some Diawara-like players will arrive, i.e. promising prospects chosen through scouting and data. Markus Krösche – if he becomes the new Head of Football, as is now almost certain – will have extensive powers in this regard.

According to recent reports, the idea of ​​making the team more Italian is there, but we know how the market works, making it difficult to proposal. Not only that, but some Italians will soon leave Milan too. Above all, Christian Comotto and Francesco Camarda are heading out on loan.

The former seems destined for Daniele De Rossi’s Genoa, while it remains to be seen where and under what terms the altter will leave. A loan with an option to buy, leaving Milan free to control the future, probably. To a small Serie A team? Possibly, but a move abroad is possible too.

Belgium and the Netherlands are countries where strikers historically have more opportunities in teams that are younger, while Germany could be another destination. If he takes a flight north, don’t be surprised.

This has now quickly been followed by a school making public that both Eddie Howe and Jason Tindall have paid them a visit.

The pair visiting Bromley High School GDST, with the school giving a rundown of what happened on the day.

The school stating: ‘Bromley High School students were treated to an unforgettable day of top flight sport as former Newcastle United Manager Eddie Howe and Assistant Manager Jason Tindall visited the school to deliver an exclusive football masterclass and an inspiring Q&A session.’.

A few snippets from their report of the day:.

Industry observers note that ‘When asked what defines a great leader, Howe emphasised that leadership begins with personal standards rather than titles. He encouraged students to focus on everyday habits, such as being the first to arrive, the last to leave and treating peers with kindness and integrity. Howe told the students, noting that trustworthiness and consistency are what truly earn the respect of teammates and classmates. Tindall echoed this sentiment, adding that genuine leadership means supporting others and leading through actions rather than words.’.

Navigating Pressure and Building Resilience.

According to recent reports, ‘Students asked how top-flight managers handle team selection, media scrutiny, and setbacks. Howe explained that he and Tindall rely on honest, consistent processes, focusing on training effort and tactical preparation rather than outside noise. He also praised Tindall’s loyalty and behind-the-scenes support, highlighting how strong partnerships rely on trust and unity even when difficult decisions are made.

Inside Diego Gomez's remarkable rise to Premier League's king of the wondergoal: Plucked from a rural Paraguayan village at 13, doing Lionel Messi's running for him at Inter Miami and starring as Brighton's aggressive machine

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1444 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 08:07 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Scattered across the flatlands of Paraguay’s deeply religious Misiones District, where families rely on the land to feed themselves through cattle ranching and cotton production, the people are idolising one of their own.
  • Diego Gomez’s ascent from the humble beginnings of a farmer’s son to the heart of a Premier League title race is a Hollywood director’s dream.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 08:07 EST, 21 November 2026.

Scattered across the flatlands of Paraguay’s deeply religious Misiones District, where families rely on the land to feed themselves through cattle ranching and cotton production, the people are idolising one of their own.

Diego Gomez’s ascent from the humble beginnings of a farmer’s son to the heart of a Premier League title race is a Hollywood director’s dream. While it is a script that has been read many times before, like an old movie or a classic song, it is also one that never gets old.

In this particular iteration, it begins on the dirt tracks of Mburika Reta, which literally translates to the ‘land of donkeys’ in Paraguay’s native Guarani, before winding through the country's capital, Asuncion, and briefly stopping among the palm-lined suburbs of Miami alongside Sergio Busquets and Lionel Messi. It is now gathering pace on England’s south coast, where Brighton find themselves in the unfamiliar territory of hunting down the Premier League champions.

In a recent development, gomez is the epitome of Fabian Hurzeler’s machine: energetic, aggressive and relentlessly forward-thinking. It is through this collective sense of selflessness that the Seagulls are second in the table, having already defeated both league leaders Arsenal and Manchester City this season. And for Hurzeler’s versatile midfielder, every performance and goal is a reminder of the moments that forged him.

‘He always told me to play forward and, when I have the ball, to have no fear,’ the 23-year-old mentioned last year of his former team-mate Messi.

Cue a spectacular goal from the halfway line against Crystal Palace last month, the Amex crowd growing feverish as the ball sailed over Walter Benitez before crashing into the back of the net.

Diego Gomez pictured as a young teen playing for Libertad (left), is now thriving for Paraguay (right) and one of Brighton's most vital players.

Gomez is congratulated by Pascal Gross after scoring a brilliant goal against Brentford.

Another rapidly followed against Brentford last weekend, with Gomez barely bringing the ball under control before hooking it into the net from 25 yards out with his supposedly weaker left foot, leaving half of his team-mates clutching their heads in disbelief.

Inevitably Gomez’s rise has not been without its setbacks. It was his mistimed tackle on Desire Doue, stretching out a leg to topple the French winger in the penalty area, that led to the heartache of Paraguay’s World Cup elimination this summer, after Kylian Mbappe slotted home the resulting spot-kick.

Yet rather than be defined by this mistake, Gomez returned home to a hero’s welcome, mobbed by locals as he was paraded through the streets of the usually sleepy San Juan Bautista in an open-top car.

‘He has the right attitude towards football,’ Hurzeler noted shortly after his arrival. ‘He loves to play. You can feel his passion in every talk with him.’.

It has been revealed that across his 10 appearances this season, Gomez has won 66 duels, more than any Brighton player. His 35 aerial duels won, second behind only Croatian centre back Luka Vuskovic, point to his impressive spring, and he has won 10 tackles, again more than any other Brighton player.

At the other end of the pitch, meanwhile, he has taken the most touches in the opposition box and has scored two goals and recorded two assists this season.

While Gomez’s physique gives the impression of a battering ram, he is surprisingly speedy, recording Brighton’s fastest top speed of the season against Chelsea at 21.01mph.

But who is this kid who was plucked out of nowhere? Who, at the age of 13, moved four hours away from his rural village to the capital to play football, navigating the bus networks as a child to get to training at FC Libertad before a move to join David Beckham’s glitzy side arrived seven years later?

Gomez, seen with his partner Geraldine Villagra, has taken an unusual route to the top.

In this case, it was Inter Miami who did the plucking, with Gomez identified by Brighton’s scouting network while he was playing in the MLS in 2024. Gomez formally joined the club as a 21-year-old in a deal worth £11million in January 2025, having agreed the move six months earlier.

Former Brighton centre back Gordon Greer is now the club’s pathway development manager and spoke regularly to Gomez during this time, travelling to Florida to see him during the latter stages of the MLS season. It’s fair to say he liked what he found.

‘We knew that he would do well because of his application,’ Greer says. ‘He was just a really talented, young, hungry footballer. You could see that he had raw potential, and I think Brighton do that really well. They sign players who have got room to improve.

According to recent reports, ‘The one thing about Diego that is really impressive is his attitude, his work rate. He’s a really driven character and he’s such a humble kid. You can ask Diego to do certain things and he’ll give it his all, no matter what you ask him to do, whether he’s good at it or not. As a coach, it must be amazing to have someone like that in your team.’.

In a recent development, during his six-month wait for the move, Gomez undertook regular English lessons, tuned in to Brighton’s games on television and spoke to Hurzeler about the areas he could improve before making the switch. All of that left him with a couple of weeks’ head start, which in Premier League terms is massive.

In a recent development, meanwhile, Brighton’s plethora of South American footballers at the time, most notably Julio Enciso, who played alongside him at Libertad, helped him settle rapidly. So too did Gomez’s girlfriend, Geraldine Villagra, who moved to Brighton to live with him, while his family regularly visit from Paraguay.

Gomez is the epitome of Fabian Hurzeler’s energetic machine for the Seagulls.

It has been revealed that spending 18 months alongside Messi, Busquets and Luis Suarez was also another important step in Gomez’s development, despite his understandable initial nerves. He forged a strong understanding with Messi on the pitch and was the engine that enabled the Argentine genius to thrive. Much like at Brighton, though, that did not stop Gomez from producing moments of magic of his own.

‘The fact that he had these superstars in the team probably helped him,’ Greer indicates. ‘We don’t have any superstars in our team like Messi, but everyone gives their all.

‘At Inter Miami, Messi was by far the best player, but Diego did a lot of the running for him and had a fantastic season in which he contributed a number of goals and assists. He just worked away at it. Regardless of the kind of environment you put him in, he finds a way through it.’.

Industry observers note that the audacity of Gomez’s two recent goals, the strike against Palace that inevitably won the Premier League Goal of the Month award for October and the Brentford one which is firmly in contention for November, almost contradicts that industrious nature. Has Greer been surprised by them?

‘He scored some really good goals for Inter Miami, but not as good as the ones he’s scored of late for us,’ he says. ‘He wants to achieve substantial things. It’s no surprise... well, it is a surprise when you see him stick one in the top corner with his left foot!’.

Gomez endeared himself to many when he broke down during a pre-World Cup press conference while speaking about the privilege of representing his country, and he remains deeply aware of where he has come from.

Earlier this year, Brighton chose to extend their UNICEF partnership to Paraguay, with Gomez becoming an ambassador for a programme that aims to develop young people's skills and confidence through sport and will reach thousands of children across the nation, a role he regards as a great honour.

After Paraguay’s elimination from the World Cup, Gomez attended one of the events in Asuncion, where he first plied his trade and where UNICEF will soon roll out the programme.

‘During his personal time, after coming back from the World Cup, he could have done lots of other things and chose instead to do that,’ Anna Easthope, Brighton’s head of marketing, adds. ‘He realises the impact of meeting kids, giving them inspiration and letting them know that sport is for everyone.’.

If a hero’s welcome followed World Cup elimination, imagine the reception a Premier League title would bring to Misiones.

Absolutely appalling abuse for Dan Burn from Newcastle United fans after he remarked this

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you hadn’t heard of Dan Burn and somebody detailed his journey in football, there is no way you would believe it.

Santiago Munez and Goal! sounds like a very believable factual documentary in comparison.

Dan Burn one of countless kids taken on by the Newcastle United Academy but don’t make it.

In his case, it was at the age of 11 when told his dream ended there.

The rest is history. Though you would be forgiven if you double checked certain facts because they sound like the work of somebody’s very active imagination.

Dan Burn who entered the world of men’s football with Darlington at non-league level, whilst working part-time collecting shopping trolleys at ASDA.

Through grit, determination and of course ability, Dan Burn developed a very decent career for himself, playing for Fulham, Yeovil, Wigan, Birmingham and Brighton.

This career not standing out as a stellar one, but certainly a very decent life in football, with a fair few Premier League appearances amongst his 300+ games across the years.

Then just over three months ahead of his 30th birthday, Dan Burn got the call that was going to change his life forever.

Inheriting a desperate mid-season relegation fight when taking the Newcastle United job in November 2021, two months later Eddie Howe was looking to bring in ready to play Premier League experienced players to avoid instant disaster for the then new Newcastle United owners.

It has been revealed that kieran Trippier, Chris Wood and Matt Targett arrived at St James’ Park in January 2022, with Brighton reluctantly allowing Dan Burn to join that trio for a reported £13m transfer fee. Eddie Howe and the Newcastle United owners were ridiculed by many journalists, pundits and fans of other clubs. Tagged as the ‘richest’ club owners in world football and yet they and their manager thought Dan Burn was the kind of signing they needed. Hilarious. Bruno Guimaraes also arrived in that same transfer window but he was aimed at the longer-term, fresh to the Premier League it would be March 2022 before he started a game for NUFC, by which point United were well on their way to safety with Burn, Targett and Wood playing key roles in that, Kieran Trippier also started well but very promptly picked up a significant injury and only returned at the very end of that season.

With relegation avoided, Eddie Howe brought in the exciting young Dutch left-footed central defender Sven Botman, who when he was 20 turning 21 played a key role in a stunning Ligue 1 title success for Lille.

Recent findings suggest that with the summer 2022 signing of Botman, I don’t think any Newcastle fan would have been surprised if Dan Burn had then ended up becoming a squad player. Instead he became a player that Eddie Howe picked every match with very few exceptions. Matt Targett picked up an injury very early that 2022-23 season and Dan Burn was moved to left-back.

The back five that played almost every Premier League match that 2022-23 season was Pope, Trippier, Schar, Botman Burn.

The ‘experts’ couldn’t believe it, Eddie Howe and Newcastle United finished fourth in the Premier League and qualified for the Champions League, plus NUFC got to their first Wembley final in 24 years.

That success was massively built on an astonishing defensive record.

Manchester City won the 2022-23 Premier League title only conceding 33 goals in the 38 league matches, this Newcastle United five matched that low goals conceded total. In the six Carabao Cup matches that got United to Wembley, only two goals were conceded across the half dozen matches.

Eddie Howe had created something very special at Newcastle United and Dan Burn was one of the first names on the team sheet, whether playing in the centre of defence or left-back.

Dan Burn finally living the Newcastle United dream in his 30s.

He was somebody the fans could really relate to, many of us kidding ourselves that if only things had worked out a little differently, that could have been you or me instead of Dan Burn in a Newcastle United shirt. That wasn’t the reality of course but that is how Dan Burn makes you feel. That he is a Newcastle United fan who by that sheer grit and determination is playing for NUFC, rather than watching them.

We have had many other homegrown heroes, many in my lifetime, but Alan Shearer had this incredible talent for scoring goals that elevated him above all others in the Premier League, whilst Peter Beardsley and Paul Gascoigne just had incredible talent that for me matches any player I have ever seen play football for any club or country.

As for Dan Burn, he has continued to be phenomenal in the colours of Newcastle United.

The 2023-24 was one of the worst ever for Newcastle United injuries, all but mission impossible for Eddie Howe and his small squad to lose so many players so often, plus the disastrous Sandro Tonali suspension. With the squad hit by so many injuries, when Dan Burn picked up a serious one to his back, he came back far earlier than the medical staff wanted him to because the manager, team and fans needed him. Newcastle United still managed 60 EPL points that 2023-24 season and came so close to qualifying from their Champions League group which was as tough as it could possibly be. One opponent reached the final and another the semi-final. United were cheated in Paris out of a famous win that would have led to them qualifying instead of PSG. In the stunning 4-1 home win over PSG, Dan Burn was immense at the back and scored THAT goal.

The finances meant Newcastle United didn’t buy any upcoming first team players in summer 2024 and indeed a PSR crisis that had to be dealt with in June 2024 meant Elliot Anderson and Yankuba Minteh were sold. Dan Burn and his Newcastle United team-mates reacted by producing the most successful season in living memory for most of us. Another Champions League qualification. Oh..and a trophy. The unforgettable sight of Dan Burn scoring the best headed goal Wembley (new or old) has ever seen. Burn one of United’s very best players that magical day, a trophy finally lifted on 16 March 2025.

Recent findings suggest that the 2025-26 season proved far too much for a still too small Newcastle United squad to cope with a 58 game season, especially as injuries piled up once again. Including Dan Burn the victim of a cowardly challenge during the away derby mix, the Geordie warrior wanted to try and play on, even though it was later discovered he’d punctured a lung and broken a rib. As always, his commitment was immense during such a challenging season.

Recent findings suggest that the perfect choice to be the new Newcastle United captain, injury delayed his 2026-27 season kicking off. No surprise that things significantly improved at the back when Dan Burn was able to start in the Premier League. After conceding 14 goals in the opening seven Premier League matches, the next three saw only two conceded (against Palace, Everton and Fulham). Then Dan Burn leading Newcastle United to Saturday’s comeback draw against an Arsenal side that had won nine of their opening ten EPL matches.

Dan Burn getting absolutely appalling abuse from Newcastle United fans.

In recent days a video has circulated online, Dan Burn stopped and asked for one of those one minute video interviews, where random questions are fired and only need a name as the answer.

I’m not sure when the video interview happened but my guess is that Dan Burn was stopped as he went into the Newcastle United Foundation dinner last week, which was to raise funds for the charity and to celebrate local achievers.

These are the questions and answers, I have changed the order in which they were asked, see if you can guess which one has prompted the abuse aimed at Dan Burn.

Best player played against – Ronaldo Funniest player – Jacob Murphy Best leader – Jordan Henderson Best finisher – Harry Kane Best on a night out – Lewis Dunk Best player you have played with – Alexander Isak Biggest prankster – David Perkins Toughest played against – Adama Traore Most famous person on your phone – Sam Fender.

It is crucial to point out that those Newcastle United fans giving Dan Burn this appalling abuse are only some Newcastle United fans, not all NUFC fans.

Industry observers note that of course I don’t know if every single one of them who are giving abuse is a Newcastle fan but certainly many of them are. As it is online you can see that they regularly post comments about NUFC and I have no doubt these people are Newcastle fans.

So just in case you were still wondering which answer has prompted all of this abuse, it is Dan Burn saying Alexander Isak is the best player he has played with.

Apparently this is an unforgivable crime, at least for some Newcastle United fans.

That this then justifies saying what a useless football player Dan Burn is AND far far worse, these fans aiming abuse at him as a person, his character.

Everybody is of course entitled to their own opinion BUT I can’t even attempt to get my head around why anyone would have this opinion AND even worse, be desperate to tell everyone else.

The best thing about social media is that everybody can now have their say.

The worst thing about social media is that everybody can now have their say.

I have no doubt that if Dan Burn sees these abusive comments he will just brush them to one side. It is just a fact that people get abuse online, especially if they are famous.

It depresses me the way many Newcastle United fans go on at times. One match, even one moment in a match, can see some Newcastle United fans giving one of our players ridiculous levels of criticism, even if they have done incredible things for the club and fans. It is like those fans who now want us to believe that Eddie Howe simply got lucky with the success he brought to NUFC, that he just stumbled along and it as all down to others why Newcastle United were suddenly winning football matches, getting to Wembley, playing in the Champions League and….winning a trophy.

This abuse for Dan Burn though, it really does my head in.

Why would any Newcastle United fan think it is appropriate?

To me, Dan Burn represents everything that is positive about Newcastle United and the people of our region.

If you asked him to run through a brick wall for Newcastle United, he would ask which one he should run through first.

Dan Burn makes me proud to be a Newcastle United fan, proud to be a Geordie.

He has been brilliant for Newcastle United, brought us so much joy, whilst off the pitch he is the same.

Countless charity events and also brave enough to talk about his mental health struggles of the past, in order to help others.

Dan Burn names the BEST player he’s ever played with 🤝🔥 https://t.co/4eqSbEhB6a.

— All Out Football (@ItsAllOutFooty) November 17, 2026.

According to recent reports, nobody is above criticism but I would love to see some Newcastle United fans just tone it down a bit. Instead of unleashing hate aimed at some of the best amongst us, have a think before giving a reaction.

Dan Burn is the real deal, a Local Hero.

Recent findings suggest that west Ham again conceded in the first half and spent the rest of the game peppering Preston’s goal – four efforts hit the woodwork but to no avail until Mavropanos’ second half equaliser. A lack of clinical finishing cost Scott Parker’s side dear as the points were shared.

Encouraging early touches with his feet and a willingness to catch rather than punch initially inspired confidence. Failed to get his fists to a corner, the ball striking Piroe on the head and looping over Herrick to give Preston a simple goal to create their lead. A superb double save just before half-time kept West Ham in touch after Mayers’ poor header. Grew in stature in the second half, notably catching balls where Hermansen might have punched.

It has been revealed that good early interplay with Bowen down the right. Unlucky not to score when his effort crashed against the post immediately after Bowen had hit the woodwork. Replaced by Souček on 78 minutes.

Solid enough first half without really being tested. Slipped in to meet a deflected Engels cross and equalise in true Mavropanos style.

Recent findings suggest that looked far more comfortable in the combative centre-back role, without being seriously tested for pace. Met Solomon’s second half cross with a header that was blocked.

Solid enough first half until a dreadful defensive header gifted the ball back to Preston, with Herrick rescuing him through a superb double save. Booked after misjudging his control and pulling down an opponent. Replaced by Scarles on 78 minutes.

According to recent reports, A great through ball released Piroe for West Ham’s first decent opportunity. Excellent work out wide, crossing with his weaker foot to allow Mavropanos to equalise. Lots of wide running in a much more advanced position than under Nuno. Looked better for it.

According to recent reports, making his first appearance of the season, revealed little sign of rustiness. Should have equalised after a well-worked corner, curling into the side-netting. Looked increasingly at home sitting in front of the defence and moving remarkably quickly across the turf. Quick feet in the opposition box led to a shot poked agonisingly close, but just wide. A pretty good shift on his return; surprising he lasted until 90 minutes, when Magassa replaced him.

Should have taken a first-time shot with his right foot, but instead shifted onto his favoured left and scuffed the chance in the first half. Needs to produce more. Evidently Parker agrees as he was replaced by Castellanos on 57 minutes.

Struck the post with a right-footed effort as West Ham pressed for an equaliser. Had the beating of his full-back in the second half, making frequent runs down the right and crossing with his weaker foot. Several shots but lacked that killer punch – as did the whole attack.

In a recent development, should have opened the scoring after ten minutes when sent through one-on-one by Engels, but the goalkeeper saved. Lots of trying and ‘nearlies’ but too little output. Booked on 82 minutes for a professional foul. Not enough from the striker.

Recent findings suggest that A decent early effort from 25 yards went straight at the goalkeeper. Immediately after the restart, stepped inside and struck the bar with a brilliant curling right-footed shot. Replaced by Solomon on 57 minutes at which point West Ham’s pace and zip largely vanished. There’s a lesson in there….

On for Austbø, 57 minutes. One jinking run inside produced a cross met by Morato’s head, but the effort was blocked. Looked very right-footed and unable to beat defenders on the outside. West Ham were poorer for the substitution of Austbø and Solomon’s introduction.

On for Mukasa, 57 minutes. Fluffed his lines on 85 minutes, looping a back-post header over the bar.

On for Mayers, 78 minutes. One decent cross late on. Understandably rusty-looking.

Spitting row mars feisty Millwall-West Ham clash

📅 19 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5425 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A spitting row marred the 100th Millwall-West Ham United derby and first for 14 years.
  • Taty Castellanos was facing trial by video after being accused of spitting on Filip Marschall during Saturday’s febrile 2-2 draw at the Den.
  • Millwall goalkeeper Marschall made the allegation to referee Paul Tierney, who was expected to include it in an official report that would then be assessed by the Football Association.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A spitting row marred the 100th Millwall-West Ham United derby and first for 14 years.

Taty Castellanos was facing trial by video after being accused of spitting on Filip Marschall during Saturday’s febrile 2-2 draw at the Den.

Millwall goalkeeper Marschall made the allegation to referee Paul Tierney, who was expected to include it in an official report that would then be assessed by the Football Association.

Spitting on an opponent is punishable with a six-match ban.

Telegraph Sport has been told West Ham striker Castellanos denies he spat on Marschall and believes he will be vindicated by video footage of the incident.

Lying little prick. Taty didn't spit ❌ pic.twitter.com/5vYxOtKqof.

Millwall manager Alex Neil said after the game that fourth official Lewis Smith had confirmed a spitting accusation had been made.

According to recent reports, asked if he had spoken to Marschall about the claim, Neil replied: “I haven’t asked him about it. But it’s like anything else; I’m sure there’ll be footage of it, or not of it, if it didn’t happen.

“I’d be extremely surprised if Fil’s made an accusation and nothing’s happened. But that’s not really for me to deal with; I’m sure the authorities will deal with that.”.

According to recent reports, west Ham manager Nuno Espírito Santo noted: “I’m aware of the allegation. I didn’t see the image; I didn’t speak with Taty. I cannot go much further on that.”.

He added: “I’m going to try to look at the images.”.

There were also ugly scenes at full time when players had to be separated at the end of a derby that had been at the centre of an unprecedented police operation.

There were six arrests as of 4pm on Saturday for offences including tailgating, assault on a police officer and entering or attempting to enter a stadium while intoxicated.

Eleven men were also arrested at around 7.15pm on Friday on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage.

The group, believed to be Millwall fans, were detained in the vicinity of a known West Ham supporters’ pub in Stratford.

Saturday’s fixture was subject to a five-mile dispersal zone, the largest ever for a football match in London, with officers granted special powers to stop and search people and vehicles without reasonable suspicion and to remove anyone causing disorder.

Riot police were out in force outside the ground, with dog units and mounted officers among 400 personnel deployed – roughly quadruple the usual number for a game there.

Those and other measures – including the use of live facial recognition, a strict segregation policy and a 12.30pm kick-off to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time – prevented a repeat of the kind of violence which has marred this fixture down the years.

West Ham fans also received a police escort to a game that saw both sets of supporters hurl foul-mouthed insults at each other throughout.

Plans to keep rival spectators apart after the match were reportedly tested by scuffles that broke out as people left the ground.

If the police were ready for a fight before the game, West Ham’s players were not as Millwall tore into them from the first whistle and dominated a first half in which they scored twice through Caleb Taylor and Camiel Neghli and hit the crossbar through a stunning 35-yard strike by Mark Sykes.

Sources indicate that MILLWALL STRIKE FIRST 🔥Caleb Taylor fires the Lions in front! pic.twitter.com/pPffYZD73D.

However, the Championship leaders finally turned up in the second half and pulled a goal back through Mohamadou Kanté before Konstantinos Mavropanos equalised with just 10 minutes to go.

ALL SQUARE at the Den 🙌West Ham equalise in the 80th minute.Everything to play for with just 10 minutes remaining 👀 pic.twitter.com/qQmDlyuQmT.

That was only after Marschall gestured that he had been spat at by Castellanos following a melee in the penalty area.

Tierney did, though, brandish a red card when Kanté pulled back Kyrell Lisbie as the substitute robbed him of the ball on the halfway line and ran clean through on goal.

The foul denied Lisbie the chance to hand Millwall their first win over their bitter rivals for 22 years, much to the frustration of fans who had roared them on from first whistle to last.

In a recent development, RED CARD 🟥West Ham are down to ten men, after Kante was sent off for denial of a goalscoring opportunity. pic.twitter.com/jRlVwLNiOs.

Describing the atmosphere as “absolutely the best by far” since he joined the club almost two years ago, Neil said: “I told the players prior to the game that this game’s a real rarity and, as a player and as a manager, it’s a privilege to be part of it.”.

Millwall: Marschall; Osei-Tutu, Taylor, Cooper, Sturge; Metcalfe (Servais 81), Mazou-Sacko (Cundle 90); Sykes (Baggott 70), Dykes, Neghli; Arconte (Lisbie 81).Booked: Lisbie 90+5.Goals: Taylor 16, Neghli 45+3.Subs not used: Batth, Crocombe, Doughty, Issoufou, Kelly.West Ham United: Hermansen; Walker-Peters (Kanté 46), Mavropanos, Kilman, Morato; Bowen, Engels, Mukasa (Austbo 68), Solomon; Piroe (Pablo 46), Castellanos (Orford 90).Booked: Morato 40, Pablo 83, Kilman 86, Mavropanos 90+5.Sent off: Kanté 89.Goals: Kanté 74, Mavropanos 80.Subs not used: Ajala, Austbo, Golambeckis, Herrick, Magassa, Scarles.Referee: Paul Tierney.

“I’m sure the referee and authorities who need to deal with it will look at it and, if it warrants it, it needs dealt with and then I’m sure they will.”.

Lisbie darts to the by-line but his cutback does not make it through the thicket of limbs and West Ham clear their lines.
