💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 22 Nov 2026 10:05.
  • Bayern Munich have been accused of putting public pressure on Jamal Musiala over his contract, with global players' union FIFPRO condemning a series of statements from senior club officials just as the Germany international returns from injury.
  • It has been revealed that the 23-year-old made his comeback during Friday's 1-1 Bundesliga draw with FC Koln after almost two months on the sidelines, but attention has promptly shifted from his return to questions surrounding his long-term future at the Allianz Arena.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 22 Nov 2026 10:05.

Bayern Munich have been accused of putting public pressure on Jamal Musiala over his contract, with global players' union FIFPRO condemning a series of statements from senior club officials just as the Germany international returns from injury.

It has been revealed that the 23-year-old made his comeback during Friday's 1-1 Bundesliga draw with FC Koln after almost two months on the sidelines, but attention has promptly shifted from his return to questions surrounding his long-term future at the Allianz Arena. Musiala signed a lucrative contract extension until June 2030 in February 2025, a deal that has now become the subject of public discussion among some of Bayern's most influential figures.

Honorary president Uli Hoeness, chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen and supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge have all addressed concerns about the midfielder's ability to regain his previous level following a difficult period of injuries and health problems.

According to recent reports, rummenigge went further after Friday's match, suggesting that Bayern might eventually have to reconsider the financial commitments attached to Musiala's contract. Those remarks prompted an unusually direct response from FIFPRO on Saturday, with the union questioning the manner in which the German champions have handled the situation.

In a statement published on November 21, FIFPRO expressed serious concern about the repeated public interventions of Bayern's senior officials, arguing that their comments had placed unnecessary pressure on a player attempting to rebuild his fitness and confidence.

The organisation described the sequence of statements as a "coordinated strategy to put pressure" on Musiala and his representatives ahead of possible contract negotiations.

FIFPRO stressed that Bayern have a responsibility to support their midfielder during his recovery and argued that any concerns surrounding his contract should be discussed privately rather than through the media.

The union also challenged the suggestion that injuries or a decline in performance could justify revisiting financial terms that both parties had already accepted.

"Contracts are there to be respected," FIFPRO declared, emphasising that contractual stability protects clubs as well as players.

Its intervention followed several weeks of public debate surrounding Musiala, who has endured a difficult period since suffering a fractured leg at the Club World Cup in July 2025. Further setbacks have restricted his involvement this season, including a hamstring injury in September that kept him out until Friday's meeting with Koln.

The midfielder has also spoken publicly about a neurological condition diagnosed after two episodes of losing consciousness during pre-season. However, that diagnosis should not be interpreted as evidence that he cannot return to elite football, and no medical conclusion about his long-term playing ability has been established.

In a recent development, FIFPRO's criticism concerns the public handling of Musiala's situation rather than any confirmed attempt by Bayern to alter his existing agreement. There has been no announcement of a salary reduction, and the union's allegation of coordinated pressure remains disputed by the club's leadership.

The controversy intensified following Rummenigge's interview with Sky Germany after Musiala's return against Koln.

The former Bayern chief executive, who remains a member of the club's supervisory board, defended the earlier remarks made by Hoeness and Dreesen, insisting that it was reasonable for Bayern to consider the financial implications of Musiala's uncertain sporting situation.

Rummenigge acknowledged that the midfielder might struggle to reproduce the performances that previously established him among Europe's most highly regarded attacking players.

Discussing a potential review of the player's financial terms, he suggested that Bayern would need to speak to Musiala, his family and his representatives if those concerns persisted.

"Then these sums would simply no longer be sustainable," Rummenigge stated, referring to the possibility of Musiala failing to regain his previous level.

He also indicated that a transfer would be difficult under those circumstances, questioning whether another club would be prepared to invest heavily in the midfielder while uncertainty remained over his recovery.

However, Rummenigge confirmed that no discussions with Musiala's representatives had taken place. He described the possibility of reviewing the contract as an idea rather than an agreed course of action, adding that Bayern intended to monitor the player's progress over the coming weeks.

Dreesen subsequently rejected FIFPRO's suggestion that the club was attempting to pressure Musiala.

"We all hope that Jamal will be the Jamal we know again," the Bayern chief executive remarked on Saturday. "He needs time to come back. We've said that several times now.".

Dreesen added that the club would assess the situation at the beginning of next year and indicated that there was no need to continue publicly discussing the player's contract.

The debate has also highlighted differing public messages from within Bayern. While senior figures have raised financial concerns, head coach Vincent Kompany and sporting director Max Eberl have expressed confidence in Musiala's ability to work his way back towards his best form.

His return against Koln was an encouraging first step after another frustrating spell on the sidelines, but a brief substitute appearance offers little basis for judging his longer-term prospects.

According to recent reports, for now, Bayern remain committed to a contract running until 2030, and any alteration to its terms would require discussions with the player and his representatives. FIFPRO's intervention has ensured that the way those conversations are approached, should they eventually take place, will attract considerable scrutiny.

Liverpool remain the favourites to beat Manchester United in Sunday's Premier League showdown despite the potential for a Mauricio Pochettino upcoming manager bounce, Didi Hamann has exclusively told Sports Mole.

Andoni Iraola's side have the honour of hosting Pochettino's Premier League homecoming at Anfield, after Man United dismissed the popular Michael Carrick during the international break.

Pochettino takes over a Man United side who start the day 19th in the Premier League table, 14 places and 10 points worse off than Liverpool, having won just one of their 10 top-flight games this season.

However, Liverpool have only prevailed in one of their five Premier League fixtures at Anfield in 2026-27, while only one of Man United's last nine permanent or interim managers has lost their first game in charge.

Nevertheless, Liverpool Champions League winner Hamann has affirmed that his former side remain the favourites due to one key reason - their more 'settled' squad - but the visit of the Red Devils is still coming at an inopportune time for the Reds.

According to recent reports, “It's certainly not the best time because Man United need a spark from somewhere," Hamann mentioned. They were going through the motions. If you look at Carrick, he's such a lovely guy, but you've got to win games if you're the Man United manager, and I'm not sure whether he believed that his team could turn things around.

"To have a manager on the sideline who comes in and makes everybody think, 'I've got to put my foot down now to keep my place and get in the team', it's certainly not the best time for Liverpool. Whether it's the worst, we'll know after the game or the weekend, but I think it's a great appointment.

In a recent development, "I always held him in very high regard. What he did at Spurs was exceptional. If you see what happened to Spurs after he left, it really went downhill year by year. It got worse. The fixture is at the wrong time.

According to recent reports, "United changed the manager at the wrong time. But it's a challenge, and there are always special games against United. The more settled side at the moment is Liverpool, there's no doubt about it. They go into the game as favourites, but they could have played them at a better time, I think.”.

Pochettino's record against Liverpool does not make for pleasant reading for Man Utd fans, though, as the Argentine has only won three of his previous 19 games vs. the Reds as a manager, suffering 11 defeats.

Comparing Iraola's start to life at Liverpool to Pochettino's statistics from his one year at Chelsea (2023-24), the current Reds boss already holds the edge in a couple of categories across all tournaments.

Pochettino collected 1.75 points per game at Stamford Bridge, while Iraola is at the moment averaging 1.94 per game with Liverpool, albeit while having taken charge of 35 fewer games.

Iraola's Liverpool also concede at a rate of 1.38 goals per game compared to Chelsea's 1.45 under Pochettino, but the Blues' 2.02 goals per game in 2023-24 marginally betters Liverpool's 2.00 in 2026-27.

Pochettino's Chelsea finished sixth in 2023-24 with 63 points, and at their current rate, Liverpool will trump the Blues' record with 68, as the hosts are averaging 1.8 points per match thus far.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules. It is a decision that, if upheld, would equate to one of the biggest scandals in football history.

City face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League. Or a combination of all, under rule W51 of its handbook. No punishment has yet been unveiled.

If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.

In a recent development, the charges can be broken down into five categories and relate to a period from 2009-23 in which City won six League Cups, three FA Cups, seven league titles and the Champions League. There is the provision for removing past titles, but that would appear remote.

City have been the dominant force in English football for most of that time, but that status is under threat with a verdict that will send shockwaves around Europe and could have huge ramifications for the club.

That is unless they can win an appeal, with sources cautioning it still may take up to another two to three years for the case to be resolved, following on from an already five-year investigation.

The Premier League’s rules provide for an independent appeal board with broad powers, including the ability to uphold, vary or overturn the independent commission’s decision.

It would therefore appear that despite the verdict, the case is far from being resolved and punishment decided. The details of the commission’s findings, when published, will be crucial to determining what happens next.

But if it is upheld, the verdict also opens up the possibility of City facing legal action from other clubs who feel they missed out on trophies and even merit money from league placings.

It is understood Premier League clubs are already discussing legal action and possible compensation claims as a result of the guilty verdict.

Industry observers note that each of those cases would have to be held individually, potentially leading to years more of litigation. Conversely, if City win their appeal, they too could take legal action against the Premier League the damage caused to their reputation.

Industry observers note that there has not yet been an official confirmation of the independent panel’s verdict from the Premier League. The Premier League declined to comment.

Sources indicate that however, several sources have told Telegraph Sport that the panel has found City guilty of all but one of the charges they faced. The one that has not been proved is stated to be one of the most serious of the 115.

Recent findings suggest that the damning verdict for City is a major new test of fragile UK relations with the United Arab Emirates, with whom bilateral trade was worth £25bn last year. Redacted freedom of information documents, seen by Telegraph Sport, show Abu Dhabi hosted UK government officials including Lord Stockwood, then investment minister, as recently as February. Khaldoon Al Mubarak, the City chairman and trusted adviser to the UAE president, was present at the meeting. Government notes from the meeting recorded that he “noted they are very proud of what they have achieved through their investments in Manchester”.

The Government previously caused acrimony among senior leaders in Abu Dhabi after putting forward legislation to ban foreign states from owning UK newspapers and news magazines. The intervention prompted the collapse of a takeover of The Telegraph in April 2024, which was largely funded by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the owner of City and vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates.

Sources indicate that the previous UK government has admitted its embassy in Abu Dhabi and the Foreign Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) in London discussed the charges levelled at City by the Premier League. However it refused to disclose the correspondence.

City have steadfastly maintained they are innocent, promising “irrefutable” evidence in support of their position, and had assembled some of the most expensive lawyers in the country to argue their case. Despite the verdict, the club are understood to be confident that it will win the argument in the end. Senior figures are said to be calm about the latest development, as significant as it seems.

According to recent reports, city rebuilt their team this summer and it is understood that signings were brought in on conventional player contracts, rather than terms including clauses triggered in the event of a heavy punishment. Given the club have consistently denied breaching financial regulations, and their deals for fresh players to work with head coach Enzo Maresca underlines their position.

On Friday, a City spokesman said: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023.

“The club have diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”.

Sources close to Pep Guardiola, the former City manager who stepped down last summer after 10 years of remarkable success at the club, including a treble triumph in 2023 and an unprecedented fourth straight league title in 2024, insist he has not been informed of any verdict.

In the days after City were first charged, Guardiola mounted a fierce defence of the club, claiming: “I am fully convinced we will be [proved] innocent.”.

The verdict vindicates the Premier League’s decision to launch an investigation after explosive allegations that City had routinely broken financial rules were first made in Der Spiegel in 2018 based on the Football Leaks documents.

Uefa previously accused City of breaches of its financial regulations and declared in 2020 that it was suspending the club from the Champions League for two years for “overstating” sponsorship revenue between 2012 and 2016.

City denied the Uefa charges and, after an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, the two-year ban was overturned. Cas found that a number of the claims brought by Uefa had fallen outside a five-year “time bar” and others were “not established”.

Sources indicate that it did, however, still impose a €10m fine after ruling that City failed to cooperate with investigators. City had previously also agreed a settlement with Uefa of €20m in 2014 following an investigation into their finances.

It has been revealed that legal experts agreed that the commission’s verdict is far from the end of the case. Yasin Patel, barrister at Church Court Chambers, noted: “City’s lawyers will now analyse this decision and look at the options open to them to appeal, which may include procedural impropriety, wrongful interpretation of law, and legal errors – importantly, they can guarantee an appeal.

“Sanctions could include a major fine, points deduction, relegation or even all three. Factoring in whether titles and trophies should be stripped, whether other clubs have been robbed of further revenue and opportunities due to City’s wrongdoings and losses incurred, we safely say that this is only the first chapter of a long-running legal saga that will not end any time soon.”.

According to recent reports, ian Hargreaves, partner with specialist disputes firm Quillon Law, noted the verdict was “not the end of the story but the beginning of a latest phase”, and added: “There is also the question of whether the panel’s decision can withstand a hard-fought appeal, and on what grounds any challenge might be brought. Much will depend on the detail of the panel’s findings and reasoning, which will inevitably be closely scrutinised by both sides.”.

Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri, who won the Ballon d’Or during his trophy-laden spell at the club, said he believed the club were innocent.

“For the players, it’s different than it is for journalists. I can understand all opinions, but we try to stay positive,” the Spain midfielder stated while on international duty.

According to recent reports, “When you see all the people who worked hard at City to achieve success, you know what we achieved can’t be taken away. It wasn’t paid for with money, but with effort and teamwork. Everything we achieved was deserved; we marked one of the great eras of English football. I believe in the club’s innocence – we already went through this in 2020.”.

Andy Burnham, the Prime Minister, mentioned: “I think we would all need to study the independent commission’s report in some considerable detail before reaching any conclusions.”.

Zohran Kwame Mamdani, the mayor of New York, posted “114” in relation to the charges while former Manchester United players David de Gea and Rio Ferdinand both asked whether they should be due winner’s medals from past seasons.

The Premier League statement in February 2023 mentioned that “a number of alleged breaches” had been referred to an independent commission. It then detailed each specific rule against each season in which the alleged breach took place. The precise number was not clear from the statement and led to varying reports between 115 and 130. Friday’s news suggested the figure was 115.

Industry observers note that all the way to 2009-10, the first full season following the club’s takeover by Sheikh Mansour, who is a member of the Abu Dhabi Royal family and the vice president of the United Arab Emirates. There were charges relating to all 14 seasons until the Premier League completed their investigation during the 2022-23 campaign. In that time, City won seven Premier League titles, six League Cups, three FA Cups and the Champions League. They have since won another league title – the first club to do so four times in a row – as well as the Uefa Super Cup, the Fifa Club World Cup and the FA Cup and League Cup double last season.

Recent findings suggest that they can be split into five groups. The biggest relates to the seasons from 2009-10 until 2017-18 and the requirement for clubs to provide accurate financial information and act in the utmost good faith.

The next set of rules concern the full disclosure of manager and player payments. The alleged manager breaches related to the period between 2009-10 and 2012-13, when Roberto Mancini was leading the team. The alleged breaches with respect to player payments relate to all of the seasons between 2010-11 and 2015-16.

According to recent reports, as well as providing financial detail, clubs were required to meet Uefa and Premier League rules which were designed to bring a club’s spending broadly in line with their income by placing set limits on losses. City were charged with breaches of Uefa’s licencing and financial fair play rules from 2013-14 until 2017-18, and the Premier League’s profit and sustainability rules from 2015-16 until 2017-18.

The final set of charges spanned the five seasons during which City were being investigated by the Premier League and rules that require members to cooperate in the utmost good faith by providing information and documents.

A full picture will only emerge when the commission publishes its findings but we know that the Premier League investigation began in December 2018 following allegations in the German newspaper Der Spiegel based on the Football Leaks documents. These included alleged payments to former manager Mancini for consultancy work at an Abu Dhabi-based club that was separate to his regular contract at City.

According to recent reports, we also know that City were alleged to have breached rules over setting out image rights payments to players in their club contract. Der Spiegel reported that the Premier League investigation also focused on payments to under-age players, as well as whether club sponsors were paying for commercial deals themselves or a significant proportion was in fact effectively coming from owner Sheikh Mansour.

City have always denied breaking any rules. In response to the Premier League statement about the alleged breaches, they said that they have “irrefutable evidence” to support their position and “look forward to this matter being put to rest once and for all.”.

In a recent development, at the start of the hearing in September 2024, Guardiola also stated: “Wait for the independent panel. We believe we have not done anything wrong.”.

Of the Football Leaks documents, City said: “We will not be providing any comment on out-of-context materials. The attempt to damage the club’s reputation is organised and clear.”.

The manner in which some players depart West Ham along with the bad feeling that develops as they press for a departure on their own terms can sometimes be the lasting memory that tarnishes their whole stay in east London.

Such was certainly the case of Marco Arnautovic, for example, a successful forward who demanded a new deal, got everything he wanted, and then quit anyway.

However, with some players, despite the bitterness, the rancorous ending of their career fades in the memory over time, and their stay is regarded more fondly for the highlights rather than the bad blood generated at the close.

Not quite sure yet which category the career and departure of Lucas Paqueta will fit into as his stay at West Ham thankfully fades into the dim and distant past.

Infuriating, gifted, inconsistent, yes, but forever remembered for ‘that’ pass to Jarrod Bowen in June 2023, Paqueta’s ‘yellow cards for bets‘ two year saga became, sadly, the other defining memory of his three years as a Hammer.

Winning the conference League title was his career pinnacle – until last weekend when he finally achieved ‘the ambition of a lifetime‘  (huh) with his boyhood club Flamengo.

Looking on the bright side, West Ham fans don’t have to endure the ‘baggage’ that came with Lucas Paquetá.

As reported by sportwitness.co.uk, West Ham’s former number ten referred merely to his time in England as ‘two very difficult years’ en route to winning the Brazilian league title:.

It has been revealed that ““I went through two very difficult years in my life. I decided to come back because I wanted this feeling, I wanted to feel welcomed, to be at the club I love.”.

Sources indicate that “I have no words to describe what I’m feeling. I arrived at this club when I was eight years old. My biggest dream was always to win trophies wearing this shirt.”.

Well done, Lucas. We’re all very happy for you.

It feels a bit like learning an ‘ex’ has got remarried. Good for them. So what? I’m so over them now….

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Italy’s U21 head coach, Silvio Baldini, has shared his thoughts on the Milan trio Alphadjo Cisse, Francesco Camarda and Davide Bartesaghi.

In a recent development, in recent years, Milan have shifted more towards giving some of their academy graduates more playing time with the first team. Bartesaghi was the first to properly get in, cementing his spot in the starting eleven last season, while Cisse has been the big breakthrough this season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Camarda has had a tougher time after a loan spell at Lecce, but Milan have made it very clear through renewals and words that they will focus more on the youngsters. It’s exciting times as well, given how they have all performed with the U21 national team too.

It has been revealed that speaking to Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, Italy’s U21 coach Silvio Baldini was asked about the breakthrough of Cisse, Camarda’s current state of mind and why Bartesaghi is a ‘luxury’ for his team. Safe to say that he likes the trio a lot.

Cisse has had a proper breakthrough. Did you see that coming?

“Compared to a year ago, I can see a different guy, who’s more mature and prepared, with higher self-esteem, psychologically changed, simply stronger.

“He has Milan to thank for signing him from Catanzaro in Serie B, believing in him and making room for him, then giving him consistent playing time. If he then makes the national team and does well, so much the better.”.

Milan deserve credit, and you also deserve credit for discovering him as a centre-forward….

In a recent development, “Analysing training sessions, a series of situations emerged where he managed to score by attacking space and depth: if you can do it on the right and left, it means you can also do it in the centre. But even there, the credit goes entirely to the staff.

In a recent development, “They had the intuition, realising that Cisse could be useful to our game system in that way and at the same time, allowing Alpha to discover a latest role successfully. I’m simply honest and meritocratic in my choices.

“Even though the goal against Armenia actually came from him as a second striker, at the end of that match we had two centre-forwards, him and Camarda.”.

Camarda, by the way, has struggled at Milan but scored for the U21s. How is that possible?

“I can only speak about the work we do together. I spoke to him at length, I dedicated time to him, I asked him to explain his concerns, his fear of not being able to express himself as he would like. I told him stories of my own life, of how I came out of it.

According to recent reports, “A dialogue not as a coach-player but as a son, or rather a grandson, as he could be, and a grandfather: from the heart. I’m not interested in performances as an end in themselves; they will come if he feels in the right place.

“I try to make him understand that I see him, I follow him in many small ways: he’s a conscientious boy who shouldn’t become obsessed with the goal, but rather experience football for what it is: fun.

“If, instead of fun, it becomes a test, then it worries you, and if you worry, you no longer enjoy it and it doesn’t help you perform at your best.”.

To have more fun, do you recommend that he should leave Milan for another team?

Recent findings suggest that “I’m not going to get involved in this. There are clubs, agents, and a family: they know what the best path will be for him. Let’s remember that he’s 18 years old, he plays for AC Milan and in the Under-21s.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s clear that the more he plays, the better it will be for AC Milan and for everyone. We’re talking about a great player, a champion in my opinion, who needs to finish his development: he’s still growing, he already has a great eye for goal, and he’s sacrificing himself for the team.”.

Camarda-Cisse: Can Milan provide the national team with one of the forward duos of the future?

Recent findings suggest that “For me, yes. I see them as a permanent fixture in the national team, and of course they need to prove it and earn it on the pitch. But they have all the characteristics to do it. I found Alpha to be better prepared, even in his game decisions. Amorim did well to develop him.”.

The third Rossoneri player is Bartesaghi: more of a full-back like with you or a winger like at Milan?

“Davide is one of the best players in his position I’ve coached in many years. He’s talented, very professional, mature, introverted yet open, and that’s not a contradiction: he has enormous potential, and he reveals it every time he comes to us.

“If I were any Serie A coach, I’d take him with me. For the Under-21s, Bartesaghi is a luxury. He plays with heart, passion, and intelligence, as well as possessing high-level technical, physical, and running skills.

“He can play in any position on the flank. In my opinion, if he starts 50 meters from the goal, he can perform at his best.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 22 Nov 2026 11:04.

Middlesbrough play host to Swansea City on Tuesday night looking to strengthen their position at the top of the Championship table.

Although the Welsh side make the trip to the Riverside Stadium sitting in eighth position, they only trail their next opponents by five points.

After a frustrating end to the fschedule before the November international break, Middlesbrough needed to use the enforced rest to reset and hope for the return of leading marksman Will Lankshear.

Encouragingly for Kim Hellberg, Boro recorded a 2-0 win over Bristol City on Saturday with their star player only being required to play 13 minutes from the substitutes' bench.

Previously, Boro had suffered a 2-0 defeat at Wrexham and were held to a goalless draw at struggling Watford when Lankshear was sidelined through injury.

Despite winning just three of their last six matches, Boro sit in top spot, helped by an eight-game unbeaten run at the Riverside Stadium.

However, Hellberg has witnessed his team concede nine times across those fixtures, something which will only encourage their opponents.

Swansea are still searching for a replacement for Vitor Matos, who has made the decision to leave for Strasbourg.

Club legend Ashley Williams is leading a four-strong interim management team, and it has already been confirmed that they will remain at the helm for this contest.

Scotland’s ramped-up second-half performance offered some cause for optimism as Sébastien Pocognoli’s tenure as head coach began with a goalless draw with Slovenia in Ljubljana.

The 39-year-old Belgian head coach, appointed in August as Steve Clarke’s successor, refreshed the side for the Nations League Group B1 opener in the Stozice Stadium, but they were fortunate on a couple of occasions at least not to fall behind before rallying before the break.

Scotland had been insipid and uninspiring for most of the first half but after the interval they played with pace and purpose as Slovenia captain and goalkeeper Jan Oblak became a key figure, making saves from Oli McBurnie and Kieron Bowie.

Oli McBurnie spurns a chance for Scotland.It remains goalless between Slovenia and Scotland.📺 Watch on BBC One pic.twitter.com/sldzhNCGGb.

“It took us a bit of getting used to in the first half, the way the gaffer wants to play,” McBurnie told BBC Scotland.

In a recent development, “We created enough chances to win the game. I should have scored. I was asked to play a different position and I enjoyed it. I’d rather be getting in the positions than not getting chances.

“Second half was a lot more of what the manager wanted from us. It was waves of pressure and the only thing missing was a goal or two.”.

However, the goal that would have made the former Union Saint-Gilloise and Monaco manager’s debut as an international boss more memorable ultimately failed to arrive.

In this extended international break, the Scots will host Switzerland at Hampden on Tuesday and then travel to North Macedonia before taking on Slovenia in Glasgow, with the Tartan Army hoping to see further improvement – and goals.

September 29: Scotland vs Switzerland.

October 3: North Macedonia vs Scotland.

October 6: Scotland vs Slovenia.

November 13: Scotland vs North Macedonia.

November 16: Switzerland vs Scotland.

Speaking to BBC Scotland, the debutant said: “Thought we struggled to get into the game first half, but second half we completely dominated the game.

“They’ve got a top goalie who made really good saves. So many positives to take and a clean sheet as well.

“We changed shape a wee bit at half-time to get more control and that did really well for us.

“It’s a substantial game again on Tuesday so it’s important to recover now and go again.

“I’ve played on the left-hand side for a couple of years now, so I’m comfortable doing that.

“We’ve had a great week. A upcoming manager, new way of playing and new faces in camp. It’s just the chances we need to take - the fact we’re creating the chances stands us in good stead.”.

The striker told BBC Scotland: “It took us a bit of getting used to in the first half, the way the gaffer wants to play.

Sources indicate that “We created enough chances to win the game. I should have scored.

“I was asked to play a different position and I enjoyed it. I’d rather be getting in the positions than not getting chances.

“Second half was a lot more of what the manager wanted from us. It was waves of pressure and the only thing missing was a goal or two.”.

Pocognoli’s first game in charge of Scotland ends in a goalless draw. The visitors produced a dominant second-half display, but their final ball and end-product was severely lacking in crucial moments. Ure, Hickey, Gilmour, McBurnie and Bowie all came close to scoring, but no one could break the deadlock.

Scotland cannot find a way past the impenetrable Oblak. There will be just two minutes of added time for the visitors to possibly score a late winner.

Recent findings suggest that lovric clatters into Gilmour and is cautioned. Slovenia can’t get out. It’s wave after wave of Scottish pressure.

Industry observers note that oblak comes out and fails to claim Robertson’s free-kick. The ball is recycled and the Tottenham full-back whips a second cross into the box and Slovenia fail to clear. Welsh is waiting for it, but lashes a first-time volley over the bar.

Karnicnik catches Robertson with a late lunging tackle and receives a yellow card, giving Scotland a chance to get the ball into the box.

The hosts make their fifth alteration of the afternoon, with Cerin withdrawn and Lovric on instead.

According to recent reports, how has Bowie missed?! Gilmour finds Bowie with an outstanding pass through the centre of Slovenia’s defence. The substitute takes a touch then scuffs a rushed finish wide. Bowie has to do better there!

Another change is here for Scotland, with Gannon-Doak on to replace Hickey.

Another substantial chance for Scotland. This time Sassuolo's Kieron Bowie goes close.Slovenia 0-0 Scotland - watch the closing stages on BBC One. pic.twitter.com/xMe5gRNgEr.

From the resulting corner, Oblak is there again to thwart McBurnie’s point-blank header. The referee then blows his whistle to relieve the pressure on Slovenia. Somehow, the scoreline remains goalless.

The hosts make another double change as Sporar and Brekalo depart for Vipotnik and Balkovec.

Recent findings suggest that welsh spots Bowie’s run and threads a perfectly-weighted pass through to the forward. From an unfavourable angle, the substitute’s one-on-one attempt is blocked by Oblak.

It has been revealed that another massive chance for Scotland! McGinn’s searching corner is met by Hickey, who flicks a header wide of the far post. Scotland’s second-half performance deserves a goal.

Pocognoli orders Scotland’s first alteration of the game, with Bowie replacing Ure up top.

Hickey finds himself very high up the pitch and tries to tee up Ure with a cushioned header, but there isn’t enough power on the pass.

Gilmour and Ure link up effectively on the counter, but the latter’s pull-back is intercepted by Drkusic.

Slovenia then make two changes as Zabukovnik and Zec replace Elsnik and Drkusic.

McGinn strides forward and tries to find Ure, but Slovenia rush back to scramble it clear. Scotland are really pushing for the opening goal.

Recent findings suggest that gilmour and McBurnie play a devastating one-two, allowing the midfielder to advance into the penalty area. He shoots and aims for the far corner, but his placed effort is collected impressively by Oblak, who makes another crucial intervention.

The second half has started as the first ended, with Scotland applying all of the pressure. Slovenia have Oblak to thank for the goalless scoreline.

It has been revealed that mcBurnie and Oblak both challenge for the ball, with the Scotsman bumping into the goalkeeper, giving Slovenia a goal kick. The decision is met by a chorus of boos from the away fans.

McBurnie latches onto a loose ball and skips away from Drkusic’s sliding challenge. One-on-one, the striker tries to round Oblak, but the Slovenian goalkeeper does sensationally to apprehend him. Upon reflection, it looks like McBurnie should have just shot and tried to put the ball between Oblak’s legs. He did the hard part, but lacked a clinical finish.

Industry observers note that mcGinn brilliantly turns Drkusic on the halfway line and then tees up Gilmour. The Napoli midfielder tries to float a pass over to the onrushing Robertson, but he hits the switch of play straight out for a throw-in. In defence of Gilmour, the pitch really doesn’t look in the best condition, with various players struggling regarding their weight of pass.

Recent findings suggest that we are back under way for the second half. Both sides are unchanged at the break.

Pocognoli’s Scotland finished the half as the better side, but an opening goal has proved to be elusive. At times, they’ve looked suspect defensively and have lacked rhythm going forward. However, Pocognoli’s squad have only been together for a few days and are playing in a upcoming system. Can they produce a more inspired second-half performance?

It has been revealed that despite Scotland’s late push for an opening goal at the end of the first half, the two sides head in level at the break. Slovenia started on the front-foot, with Sporar and Drkusic both going close for the hosts, before Ure struck the post to be denied a dream debut goal.

HALF TIME: Slovenia 0-0 Scotland.No goals at the break in Ljubljana.#SVNSCO pic.twitter.com/6VGFRprBiz.

According to recent reports, ure strikes the woodwork! The Sevilla striker is agonisingly close to a debut goal for his country. He cuts inside to work some space and fires a low effort at goal, but his shot hits the post.

Scotland's best chance of the game so far 😯 Sevilla striker and debutant Robbie Ure strikes the post just before half-time.However, it remains goalless at the break.📺 Watch Slovenia v Scotland on BBC One 🇸🇮 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 pic.twitter.com/fm1wH2fOej.

Much better from Scotland! McGinn turns his marker and clips a wonderful pass over to Ure, who has drifted out wide. Hickey is arriving to pounce on the loose ball, but the wing-back’s effort is blocked by the Slovenian defence.

Robertson picks up the game’s first yellow card for an off-the-ball incident. The Scotland captain is clearly very unhappy with the decision as we await to see a replay. Nevertheless, the action resumes with a Slovenia free-kick.

Sources indicate that slovenia go close again as a corner is whipped in. Drkusic wins the header at the near post and it bounces off the outside of the near post. That is definitely another warning sign for Scotland.

Matko goes on the outside of Welsh, and from a tight angle, he shoots, but his fizzed effort saves the side netting of the near post. Some fans behind the goal cheer because they think it’s gone in, but their view has really deceived them.

It has been revealed that it’s been a quiet afternoon for both goalkeepers so far, with neither yet to make a noteworthy save. On a couple of occasions, Slovenia have had encouraging opportunities to get the ball into the Scotland’s box, but the deliveries have been overhit and poorly executed.

Recent findings suggest that similarly to Scotland, Slovenia are also playing a tremendously high-line. Unlike Slovenia, Scotland have been unable to find the right pass in behind the home side’s defence. Gilmour then carelessly gives the ball away as Scotland’s latest spell of possession ends.

Since Slovenia wasted that 14th-minute chance, Scotland have grown into the contest and are beginning to look comfortable in possession. However, they’re still waiting to craft their first notable opening here.

According to recent reports, the hosts miss a huge chance! Once again, Sturm gets in behind Scotland’s incredibly high line and then fires a low cross into the penalty area. Sporar then beats McKenna to the delivery, but taps his close-range effort wide of the far post from inside the six-yard box. That’s a massive let-off for Scotland...

Recent findings suggest that matko is unleashed by a drilled pass then pierces through a gap between Robertson and Welsh. The Slovenia winger drives into the penalty area and tries to find either Sturm or Sporar with a cross, but Hendry does magnificently to make a last-ditch clearance.

Slovenia have the ball in the net, but the offside flag is up. Sturm gets in behind Scotland’s defence and slides a low cross into Sporar’s path. The striker then sweeps a composed first-time effort into the top corner. It’s a brilliant finish, but Sturm was miles offside in the build-up.

In a recent development, gunn comes out confidently to collect a looping cross, before the ball is released forward in McBurnie’s direction. The Hull City striker and Ure are playing really close to each other, very much like an old-school front-two.

Recent findings suggest that slovenia forward Sturm is wiped out by Hendry’s wild early challenge. The Scotland defender is perhaps lucky to avoid a booking. Welsh then heads the resulting set-piece away and out for a corner.

Sources indicate that the hosts get us underway in the Slovenian capital. Can Pocognoli begin his Scotland tenure with a Nations League victory?

Recent findings suggest that both teams are out on the pitch in Ljubljana. We are moments away from the start of the Pocognoli era.

On paper, it looks like Sebastien Pocognoli has opted for a five-back formation, with Swansea City defender Stephen Welsh making his Scotland debut as one of the centre backs.

A upcoming-look attack is spearheaded by the returning Oli McBurnie and 22-year-old Robbie Ure, who like Welsh, will also make his Scotland debut.

Angus Gunn remains his country’s first-choice goalkeeper.

Industry observers note that debutants Robbie Ure and Stephen Welsh are each poised for their first international cap. Billy Gilmour returns to the starting XI after missing the World Cup through injury and Oli McBurnie will make his first appearance for Scotland since 2021.

“The first game is always a special game so you have to bring the mental aspect in for the players and for the staff.

“A good result can help but the most important thing is we see things that we work on through the week. I hope is we apply that well then we will get the result which will be the perfect mix.

According to recent reports, “I hope we can bring a good game, and a good exciting principle on the pitch. I think we need the support from the supporters because there’s a lot of upcoming players.

In a recent development, “We need to create a good energy but it’s up to us on the pitch to create this. So then we can be hand in hand with the supporters.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this UEFA Nations League B, Group 1 match as Slovenia host Scotland at Stozice Stadium in Ljubljana.

According to recent reports, scotland qualified for their first World Cup in 28 years this summer, but they exited the tournament with a whimper after failing to finish as one of the best third-place group sides. Steve Clarke’s men beat tournament debutants Haiti 1-0 in their opening match, before falling to defeats without scoring against Morocco and Brazil.

Following the World Cup, Clarke stepped down as Scotland’s head coach, ending a seven-year tenure, and was replaced by Belgian manager Sebastien Pocognoli. The former Monaco boss will take charge of his first game in his new role today and will be itching to make an encouraging start in a new era for Scottish football.

Over this extended international break, Pocognoli’s side will also face Switzerland and North Macedonia, as well as a return fixture against Slovenia in Scotland on October 6 to round off a busy period.

While Scotland took part in the World Cup, Slovenia were reflecting on their hugely disappointing qualification performance, where they finished third in their group behind Switzerland and Kosovo without winning and netting just three goals across six matches.

Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko – Slovenia’s star man and most well-known player – withdrew from Bostjan Cesar’s squad earlier this week after the recurrence of a shin injury caused the 23-year-old to completely miss the 1-1 draw against Fulham last Sunday.

Scotland have a few notable absences, with Scott McTominay, Che Adams and Lawrence Shankland all unavailable, but Billy Gilmour returns to the fold after missing the World Cup through injury, Oli McBurnie has been recalled and Sevilla striker Robbie Ure has received his first senior call-up.

Kick-off is at 14:00, with team news coming shortly.

Arsenal backup goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga is poised to make just his second Champions League appearance for the Gunners in Tuesday's league-phase clash with Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates.

Mikel Arteta lost David Raya to a shoulder injury in Saturday's 2-2 Premier League draw with Newcastle United, although it is still not clear how serious the Spaniard's problem is.

Raya's concern is not serious and he could even return against Manchester City at the weekend, but Kepa will at least step in here, 10 months after making his UCL debut for Arsenal in January's 3-2 victory over Kairat Almaty.

While Kepa for Raya is an enforced change on Arsenal's end, Arteta could make two more unenforced alterations at the back, swapping out Jurrien Timber and Riccardo Calafiori for Ben White and Piero Hincapie respectively.

William Saliba was on the bench for the first time in a Premier League game this season at St James' Park, but as he is still yet to play a single minute of senior football this season, Ezri Konsa should be preferred from the first whistle.

The latter's England teammate Myles Lewis-Skelly can also anticipate a start over Bruno Guimaraes, but there should be no respite for Declan Rice against the current Bundesliga leaders.

The in-form Noni Madueke, Martin Odegaard and Eberechi Eze are likely to be retained in attack too, but the more open nature of Champions League games could benefit Viktor Gyokeres over Kai Havertz after the former's goal and assist vs. Slavia Prague, meaning a total of five changes from Arteta.

Bukayo Saka (quad) and Martin Zubimendi (hamstring) remain out for the Premier League champions.

Arsenal possible starting lineup:.

Kepa; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapie; Lewis-Skelly, Rice; Madueke, Odegaard, Eze; Gyokeres.

The numbers alone are astonishing. Nine wins on the bounce for the first time in their history, their victory here against Nottingham Forest making it six on the spin at home at an aggregate score of 15 to nil. Five wins in a row in the Premier League for the first time, too, a result that moved them into the top four.

Recent findings suggest that this is Bournemouth, remember. Only this is Bournemouth now.

Industry observers note that make no mistake: this is no hot streak. This is not a team under Marco Rose carried to win after win after win on a wave of momentum and vibes. This is relentless, breathtaking stuff. This is a team that, week after week, outplays every team that stands in front of them. It doesn’t matter if it’s Forest, or Manchester United, or AC Milan. Bournemouth turn up and they blow their opponents away.

They move it quicker and sharper, they win it back faster and higher. They give teams no time to think or breathe, so it’s little wonder they have no answer.

Sources indicate that ‘We never really struggled, stated Rose. 'We suffered a little bit at the end, but we defended quite well together, and that's why it's a deserved win.

Bournemouth racked up their sixth successive league victory and ninth in all competitions.

It has been revealed that 'If we use the right approach every game – and this is really, really demanding – we win games. Next game, we have to prove it again. If we do it, then we can keep the level up. But as I said, this is a tough job.

Sources indicate that ‘The collective is strong, but even this we have to maintain. Because if you win games…I mean, some of our players right now are in a lot of noise and rumours.

'If we are able to keep these kinds of things away from the locker room, and if everyone comes into training every day, works hard and gives everything for the club and the team, then we are really, really good.'.

The only real surprise was that Evanilson, Bournemouth’s talismanic Brazilian, didn’t leave with more than just his one, now customary, goal.

That itself was another fine finish after Tyler Adams won the ball high up the pitch – obviously – dinked it across to James Hill, back after his first England call-up, who flicked a header into Evanilson’s path. He thumped it past Matz Sels to do the rest.

In a recent development, rose, who called him a ‘real No9’ the other week, had been urging him to get into the box more to finish off chances. He did that, all right. Twice earlier in the game, he raced on to through balls only to be denied by Sels and a last-ditch tackle from Jair Cunha.

His opening strike, his eighth goal in his last nine games, means he is the first Premier League player to reach double figures for goal contributions with six goals alongside his four other assists. He leads the press, he creates chances, he scores goals. He does the lot.

In a recent development, that’s now six league games in a row he’s found the net, halfway to breaking Jamie Vardy’s record of 11 in a row. You wouldn’t put it past him.

Bournemouth’s talismanic Brazilian Evanilson scored for the sixth successive league match.

Sources indicate that forest came into this, after all, off the back of a huge, much-needed victory against Manchester City. After just one win in Oliver Glasner’s opening nine league games, that was the performance those around Forest felt that could spark the season into life.

It was also meant to be the one where Liam Delap’s Forest career burst into life with two thunderous goals in a bullying, battering-ram showing.

Alas, they both ran into a proper team this week.

Forest tried to go direct to Delap, partly to try to bypass the intense Bournemouth press, but nothing stuck. Delap lost possession with 23 of his 39 touches. He committed more fouls than he had shots and found his way into the referee’s book for clumsily bundling over Adam Smith.

It has been revealed that the visitors huffed and puffed in the second half but never really looked like scoring. The closest they got was a couple of speculative long-range efforts from Morgan Gibbs-White and James McAtee before a late goalmouth scramble nearly provided an opening through chaos more than creativity.

It was only the busy hands of Sels that kept the scoring respectable.

Industry observers note that ’The defeat was deserved,’ stated Glasner. ‘City and today were completely different. It's like a different sport. This is football, but it's different.

In a recent development, 'When teams play like City, when it's more of a tactical game, we are doing well. When it's more of a physical, intense game, we're struggling. Today our weaknesses came to the surface.’.

Sources indicate that when asked if he had the players to play this way, Glasner responded: 'Right now, I have to say no. If not, we will add players. If we believe we need somebody to add this physicality, these quick solutions, we will do it.'.

Did they expect much else, though? Forest never beat Bournemouth. That’s 13 meetings in a row now they have failed to win.

‘Nottingham Forest, it’s happened again,’ sang the home fans in the final few minutes.

Liam Delap and Nottingham Forest crashed into a proper team as they came back down to earth after their win over Man City before the international break.

Marcus Tavernier's performances could get a chance with England if he maintains his form.

According to recent reports, bournemouth have already had a couple of deserved England call-ups this season in Hill and midfielder Alex Scott. How long until Marcus Tavernier gets his chance?

No English player has scored more Premier League goals this season than the Bournemouth winger, level with Morgan Rogers and Dominic Calvert-Lewin, and once again he was at the heart of everything good the Cherries do.

His superb cross behind the Forest defence found Justin Kluivert for Bournemouth’s second of the afternoon. He danced through the Forest defence to set up Rayan for a late chance.

'It was my 11th Premier League game today, and I couldn't see better offensive midfielders so far this season,’ said Rose.

In a recent development, ‘If you see how he works and how he plays, the quality he has, he scores goals. He's 27, he's at the best age.

‘If he plays well, if he stays healthy, I think, like with Hilly, these things come. They're just around the corner.'.

Gerry Cardinale had a meeting with the AC Milan management at Casa Milan yesterday, during which there were four key topics, according to reports.

Cardinale has arrived in the city in good time for Milan’s game against Frosinone tomorrow. Yesterday, there was a summit with the Milan management, including the CEO Massimo Calvelli, Head of Football Intelligence Bobby Gardiner, and Head of Recruitment Tiago Estevão.

Industry observers note that this was reported by Sky Italia (via MilanEye) and various outlets, highlighting how Cardinale wants to be ready for the January window and even the summer window. Markus Krösche will be there to help him with that, set to be declared next week, as Gazzetta dello Sport reported.

According to Daniele Longo, there were four key topics during the meeting: the renewal of Adrien Rabiot (which is close), the Endrick pursuit (which is heating up), Goncalo Inacio for the defence, and Krösche’s announcement.

There could be a lot of major movement in the coming months, in other words, as Cardinale is really pushing for these things to materialise. Of course, other matters were also discussed during the meeting but as Longo highlighted, those mentioned above were the main ones.

Cardinale will be at Milanello today and then he will also be in the stands for the game tomorrow, showing his support for the team yet again.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Separated by just one point but nine places in the Champions League rankings, Arsenal and Borussia Dortmund cross paths in Tuesday's league-phase encounter at the Emirates Stadium.
  • The Gunners boast a marginal advantage over their German counterparts, having taken 10 points from their opening four fixtures against Napoli, Bayern Munich, Lille and Slavia Prague.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 22 Nov 2026 11:57, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 16:25.

Separated by just one point but nine places in the Champions League rankings, Arsenal and Borussia Dortmund cross paths in Tuesday's league-phase encounter at the Emirates Stadium.

The Gunners boast a marginal advantage over their German counterparts, having taken 10 points from their opening four fixtures against Napoli, Bayern Munich, Lille and Slavia Prague.

Meanwhile, Niko Kovac has guided Dortmund to victories over Real Betis, Sabah FK and Villarreal, albeit while also overseeing a dampening 1-0 defeat away to Bodo/Glimt on matchday two.

Here, Sports Mole takes an in-depth look at the head-to-head record and previous meetings between the two sides.

From eight previous Champions League meetings between Arsenal and Borussia Dortmund, the North London giants hold the bragging rights, but only just.

Indeed, the Gunners have won four of their eight head-to-heads compared to three for BVB, while only one previous encounter has ended all square.

The 2002-03 season marked the inaugural competitive meetings between Arsenal and Dortmund, who each got one over the other in the group stage; the Gunners triumphed 2-0 at Highbury as Dennis Bergkamp and Freddie Ljungberg netted in the second half, before Dortmund prevailed 2-1 at home, courtesy of a winner from future Arsenal fan favourite Tomas Rosicky.

Not until the 2011-12 season would the two teams butt heads again, but they were subsequently drawn to face each other in three of the next four Champions League group-stage campaigns.

Dortmund and Arsenal drew 1-1 at Signal Iduna Park in September 2011, but Arsene Wenger's men prevailed 2-1 at the Emirates two months later thanks to a Robin van Persie brace.

Both sides then beat each other away from home for the first time in the 2013-14 campaign, Dortmund earning a 2-1 Emirates triumph before Arsenal won 1-0 in Germany, Aaron Ramsey nodding home the only goal.

The 2014-15 campaign also saw Arsenal and Dortmund trade blows and victories, as Jurgen Klopp inspired BVB to a 2-0 success at the Westfalenstadion, before Yaya Sanogo and Alexis Sanchez sealed an identical Gunners win in North London.

Arteta captained Arsenal to victory in their November 2014 Emirates showdown, but that would prove to be the Spaniard's final senior appearance of that season, as he picked up a serious calf injury in the second half before also undergoing ankle surgery.

Nov 26, 2014: Arsenal 2-0 Borussia Dortmund (Champions League).

Sep 16, 2014: Borussia Dortmund 2-0 Arsenal (Champions League).

Nov 06, 2013: Borussia Dortmund 0-1 Arsenal (Champions League).

Oct 22, 2013: Arsenal 1-2 Borussia Dortmund (Champions League).

Nov 23, 2011: Arsenal 2-1 Borussia Dortmund (Champions League).

Sep 13, 2011: Borussia Dortmund 1-1 Arsenal (Champions League).

Oct 30, 2002: Borussia Dortmund 2-1 Arsenal (Champions League).

Sep 17, 2002: Arsenal 2-0 Borussia Dortmund (Champions League).

Industry News: England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation

📅 26 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 32 min read (6407 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~32 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that there had been so much talk – first raised by Thomas Tuchel after the shocking World Cup exit to Argentina – about England’s DNA.
  • In a recent development, the world and European champions were England’s first opponents – after the World Cup – in this Nations League campaign and came away from Wembley with a deserved win.
  • It has been revealed that mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that there had been so much talk – first raised by Thomas Tuchel after the shocking World Cup exit to Argentina – about England’s DNA. About whether they could keep the ball, pass the ball, control the ball, the way Spain do.

In a recent development, the world and European champions were England’s first opponents – after the World Cup – in this Nations League campaign and came away from Wembley with a deserved win. They are now 39 games unbeaten with substitute Mikel Oyarzabal, who scored the winning goal against England in the final of the last European Championship, doing so again.

It has been revealed that mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN! 🎯Spain retake the lead after a slick finish from the Spaniard 👏#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pPT3KvRHWl.

Recent findings suggest that that may have been no surprise, even if the inevitable “olés” after Spain’s third goal will have hurt. But the nature of it? For the England manager this was another shocker. Not in the way his team went about the task. They were positive, fun, attacking. But in the way they conceded – goals and chances – and lost.

According to recent reports, on this performance, DNA, for England, stands for Defensively Not Able, as they threw away what could have been a famous and restorative victory. Instead, with Croatia beating the Czech Republic in the other group game, England are under immediate pressure to win in Prague on Tuesday.

It has been revealed that in fact, England have conceded 13 goals in their past six matches – in fairness including four in that third-place World Cup 6-4 win over France – and that is not good enough for a top-tier nation. Tuchel needs to sort it out defensively.

It has been revealed that it could have been very different if Harry Kane had not missed from the penalty spot, slipping as he struck the ball, with England improbably 2-1 ahead. “It would have been the decisive punch,” Tuchel stated. Maybe so, even if there was always the feeling that Spain could go through the gears.

Industry observers note that kane MISSES from the penalty spot! 😧Harry Kane slips when he strikes the ball, let off for Spain and Luis de la Fuente#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pvg3GGa9ma.

Afterwards there were claims, led by the impressive Anthony Gordon, that this was a missed opportunity for England. A bit like the World Cup. They need to shake this theme.

The irony was this was one of their best creative displays for quite some time. They took the game to Spain and could have scored more. And conceded more.

In truth it could have been Spain 4 England 0 inside half an hour and before Tuchel’s team laid a glove on their opponents.

Another let off for England 😧Ferran Torres misses another big chance one-on-one with James Trafford #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/KFkJoJUW6c.

The manager had also spoken about how England should “embrace the chaos” as their best route to success. That may appear a questionable tactic – does chaos ever win a tournament? – but England certainly did that. This was as chaotic and, admittedly, entertaining as it gets.

In a recent development, england attacked with pace and power with the pick of their players the two based in Spain: Gordon, who scored, and Jude Bellingham. And the defenders? This was a bad night for Marc Guéhi, his Manchester City team-mate Nico O’Reilly (cue speculation about whether they were distracted by the verdict on the Premier League charges against their club) and for Jarell Quansah at right-back who is so evidently a centre-half.

Sources indicate that A penny, once more, for the thoughts of the unused Trent Alexander-Arnold. The fourth defender, Ezri Konsa, vented his frustration at what was happening around him.

It was not just the errors but the unforced nature of them. Poor in possession with misplaced passes and defensively wide open. There is a gap between Spain and England but not as big as the gaps that were exposed in England’s back four. They endured a full house of calamities. They seemed strangely unaware – or incapable of dealing with – the danger posed by the outstanding Lamine Yamal.

Maybe because of the opposition – or the criticism – England felt the need to play out. But what an horrific start. What an inexplicable moment for Guéhi as he received the ball from O’Reilly and turned into trouble, gifting possession to Yamal who ran on and scored. Inside two minutes.

WHAT A START FROM SPAIN 🇪🇸Lamine Yamal pounces on a Marc Guéhi error to give Spain an early lead at Wembley #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/Et83EyTPlp.

Spain walked out with the second star on their shirt – to mark their second World Cup triumph. That was the star Tuchel had promised for England.

Now, straight away, they were up against it. It could have turned very ugly. Ferran Torres, who had scored the winner in the World Cup Final, had one disallowed for offside, then was thwarted by James Trafford after – inexplicably again – being played onside by Quansah.

BIG SAVE from James Trafford 🧤The Leeds United goalkeeper keeps out Ferran Torres#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/nj5b8AUSQU.

Then Torres was sent clear following Elliot Anderson’s poor pass, only to drag his shot wide. The third miss came from Dani Olmo, again set up by Yamal.

It could – it should – have been game over. Then England unexpectedly turned it around. They had kept attacking despite what was going on at the back and struck through a truly thrilling counter-attack, with Gordon and Bellingham combining before the Barcelona winger calmly beat goalkeeper Unai Simon.

Sources indicate that ENGLAND ARE LEVEL! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿A brilliant finish from Anthony Gordon after a breathtaking counter attack 👏#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/z0nSfWIHVd.

It was an exceptional goal and was quickly followed by a fortunate one as O’Reilly’s cross was met by Kane who stooped to steer in a header, only for it to strike Marc Cucurella, who made a mess of clearing, and it went past Simón.

I think we'll give that goal to Harry Kane 🎯England come from behind to lead Spain thanks Harry Kane, with assistance from Marc Cucurella ⚽️#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/X3qSOWUhVT.

The Spain left-back hit the post with a cross, misjudged by Trafford who was given this game and the next to stake his claim ahead of Jordan Pickford who has so long been the undisputed first-choice.

England dominated for a while and Bellingham won a penalty, after a VAR intervention, only for Kane to strike the crossbar.

It has been revealed that how Spain made them pay and worryingly so. O’Reilly passed the ball straight to Olmo who swept it inside. Substitute Álex Baena checked and beat Trafford from the edge of the area. Even worse was how Spain cut through the heart of England defence with Baena finding Oyarzabal. Why was no defender closer to him? What was Guéhi doing? And O’Reilly? Oyarzabal exquisitely dinked the ball over Trafford.

Thomas Tuchel does not think Manchester City’s guilty verdict over almost all of their Premier League charges distracted his England players in the Nations League defeat to Spain.

City players Marc Guéhi and Nico O’Reilly were at fault for two of Spain’s goals and both Tuchel, the head coach, and England captain Harry Kane confirmed news of the verdict had been discussed among the squad.

Tuchel does not strategy to address the issue with his players ahead of the remaining Nations League games against Czech Republic and Croatia.

Recent findings suggest that asked if the City verdict had been a cause of discussion ahead of the Spain game, Tuchel replied: “Not for me, but I can imagine maybe for the Man City players. I won’t comment on it as it’s an ongoing case.

Sources indicate that “I didn’t make it a topic. It was not a topic for me. I’m just thinking about Spain and the team and meetings. The players have more time than me. So I can imagine they talk about it. It’s good they do. I don’t think it was a distraction for them.”.

Kane added: “There was a discussion, but when we’re with England, we kind of put club football to one side and it was no different this week.”.

Tuchel also refused to point the finger of blame at Guéhi, O’Reilly or Kane, who missed a penalty, for England’s defeat despite admitting his team got off to the worst possible start by conceding a goal after two minutes.

“We will focus on the positives, but also highlight the stuff we can do better,” Tuchel said. “Not even speaking about individual mistakes because this is normal. It just happens. It should not happen, and for sure not in this amount. But there is no sense in showing the individual mistakes or telling them ‘please don’t make mistakes’. That is normal, but we can do things better. We can defend the third goal better. But we will focus on the positives. There is a lot to take away from the game.

“We wanted to be the team desperately to beat them [Spain] and we think we had them. We still think we had them at half-time. That was the way the team showed up after half-time. So we will focus on that, but the reality is we lost and the reality is we need to prove it again.”.

“It was a terrible start, the worst possible start, which makes it so difficult against a team like this. The reaction was very good. After 10/12 minutes, we were the better team but we gave away too many mistakes. We were the better team. If we had converted the penalty, it could have been the decisive moment. We have to keep going and learn from the mistakes. We could have created more if we had been more clinical in the final 20 metres. We showed great bravery and courage with our high-ball wins. There will always be moments you suffer against teams like this. The effort and quality were there tonight but the result does not prove it today.”.

“I think there is a gap [between Spain and England]. They [Spain] are the world champions and European champions. Mikel Oyarzabal was never going to miss. He was always in control of the situation. Honestly, people talk about sexy football, that is sexy football. I would watch that all night.”.

Harry Kane wants England to address how they lost their identity and went “against our beliefs” at the World Cup.

In a brutally honest assessment of the tournament, the England captain admitted Thomas Tuchel’s team did not play to their full potential in several games – even before the painful semi-final exit against Argentina.

Kane, who played golf instead of watching the World Cup final, revealed the 2-1 Atlanta defeat hurt more than missing a penalty four years earlier in Qatar, when England were knocked out by France in the quarter-finals.

Recent findings suggest that “This one hurt more than any other one. I would probably say even more than when I missed a penalty in Qatar because of the manner that it happened,” Kane said. “It was not us as a team.

In a recent development, “We trust our players and the player know very well that if you miss a camp then someone plays well in your position that the competition is always on. You have to make sure to be available and to produce top-level performances in camp and if you do so, that counts for something. Right now, it is not on my list of worries. I am not wired like this. From the moment I arrived at SGP my full focus is 100 per cent with the players who are here.

“There is no threat, distrust or threat of consequences. It will come naturally. I truly believe that we have the opposite. You will talk to our captain, Harry Kane, who has the most minutes for club and country and is happy to be here while teammates of his are enjoying a 10-day break. He is the role model and that is the vibe we have here.”.

They do have plenty to cheer about:.

James Trafford is poised to start for England ahead of Jordan Pickford against Spain tonight.

Pickford has been England’s No1 for eight years but Thomas Tuchel is set to make a change to face the world champions in the Nations League opener at Wembley.

Trafford went to the World Cup in the summer and has started the Premier League in good form following his move to Leeds.

In the first match since the World Cup, changing his goalkeeper is a major selection decision from Tuchel.

Elsewhere, Jarell Quansah is set to play at right-back ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold while Myles Lewis-Skelly is also in line to return to the starting XI after being recalled into the squad after missing the World Cup.

Sources indicate that england begin their Nations League campaign with a home game against the world champions Spain. This is England’s first game since the World Cup, with their dreams of glory ended by Argentina in the semi-finals, but they did finish third after beating France in a high-scoring third/fourth play-off. The last meeting between these sides saw Spain beat England to win Euro 2024. They also faced off in the Nations League back in 2018, with Spain winning at Wembley and England taking victory over in Spain.

England’s plans for these games has been disrupted by a number of withdrawals. Cole Palmer had earned a recall having been left out of the World Cup squad but the Chelsea forward has withdrawn due to a minor injury, despite playing the full game for Chelsea against Brentford in the final game before the international beak.

It has been revealed that “He [Palmer] plays with discomfort and pain and cannot play on the highest level with discomfort and pain,” Tuchel said. “Chelsea informed us. That is my understanding. We are not managing load. This is not an ‘international break’. It is a competitive environment, where the players love to train and be together. That is what we created. We will never compromise on that. We will never let this feeling creep in that the players do not want to come [to England camps]. We focus on the guys who absolutely want to play for England.

According to recent reports, “For sure it is a missed opportunity. It is another missed opportunity. He misses too many opportunities. I do not blame him for it, it is just a fact. He misses way too many camps with injuries. I only want to rely on what I personally witness and see within my team. For that you have to be in camp. If you are not in camp there is a next level to impress that you cannot achieve because you can only do it with me on the pitch and with us on the pitch. It is a missed opportunity.”.

Industry observers note that declan Rice has also withdrawn from the squad despite playing the full game in Arsenal’s defeat to Brighton as have Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento. Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner have been called up as a result.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is back in the fold for the first time since June 2025. 18-year-old Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha made his England debut against Fresh Zealand during the World Cup warm-ups and takes his place in this squad, although he does make the matchday squad for tonight’s game. England will also take on Czechia, Croatia and then Cezchia again during this international break.

Having been crowned world champions back in July, Spain are now champions of both Europe and the world. Back in June 2025, Spain made the Nations League final but lost on penalties to Portugal. Ahead of this international window, The Royal Spanish Federation has extended Luis de la Fuente’s contract until 2032. After tonight, Spain will host Croatia and Czechia before travelling to Croatia to cap off this international window.

In a recent development, this is an extended international break, with four games to take place during this window. Team news from Wembley to follow shortly.
