Antonelli is still disputing the lap deletion over team radio but his team tell him the images show he exceeded track limits. This is now a lot of pressure on the championship leader; any mistake now and he will not make Q3. His teammate Russell is only in seventh.

Recent findings suggest that antonelli was fourth fastest but has had his lap time deleted for exceeding track limits at turn six. That is a substantial moment in Q2 and could prove problematic if he gets into Q3. Antonelli appeared to be confused when he was told about his lap deletion over team radio but the on-board view looked pretty clear-cut.

Piastri then comes across the line in third.

Here's the moment Kimi ran wide 👀#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/E0VdWdBt8x.

The Dutchman looks in a great spot at the moment to take pole position today and his 1:35.696 is very quick. He is nearly four tenths quicker than Antonelli.

How about the Ferraris? Leclerc was quickest in the middle sector but is nearly three tenths down on Verstappen. Hamilton puts himself into third place. Russell is more than half a second down on Verstappen.

In a recent development, verstappen has been shown a black and white flag for driving unnecessarily slowly. I doubt he will get a grid penalty for that but it will be a warning for the Dutchman.

Anyway, the drivers, other than Colapinto and Alonso, are on flying laps, with Verstappen currently fastest inthe first sector.

The green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and the second part of qualifying is under way. Like the start of Q1, it is hardly a stampede to go out.

Industry observers note that 17. Nico Hulkenberg (Audi)18. Oliver Bearman (Haas)19. Esteban Ocon (Haas)20. Alex Albon (Williams)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac).

Recent findings suggest that the Aston Martin of Stroll improves significantly from 20th and is set to make Q2, as is his teammate Alonso. A bit of a surprise to see the Aston Martins improve and make it into Q2.

Go Fernando! 🤩 Go Lance! 🤩First double Q2 appearance this season 🙌#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/xjiWYv6ycr.

That has seen the Audi of Hulkenberg drop into the drop zone and the German is out. For contrast, his teammate improves to go into eighth place! Hulkenberg had a major lock up into turn 14, which proved very costly.

Recent findings suggest that as it stands, eight of the top nine are remaining in the garage. Russell is in ninth and has not gone out but Gasly above him in eighth has. You would imagine Russell is perfectly safe.

In a recent development, 17. Esteban Ocon (Haas)18. Alex Albon (Williams)19. Oliver Bearman (Haas)20. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac).

Ocon, in 17th, is quite far off Hulkenberg in 16th and needs more than four tenths to usurp him.

The screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he notes Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

In a recent development, it’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

“Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he said. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external tech giant who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

He added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”.

In a recent development, the two Ferraris are on medium tyres but Leclerc still puts himself into second place. He is then displaced by Hamilton, who slots in behind Verstappen. Good times from the Ferraris on the mediums.

Recent findings suggest that what about the McLarens? Norris goes sixth fastest but is more than six tenths down on Verstappen. Then comes Piastri, who goes fourth fastest, just under four tenths off Verstappen.

Arguably the three favourites for pole; Antonelli, Russell and Verstappen, are all on flying laps.

The first sector goes the way of Verstappen, who is purple, and then the Dutchman goes purple in the middle sector.

Antonelli is two tenths faster than his teammate Russell but Verstappen is over half a second quicker than the Mercedes. Hadjar is then second fastest to show the pace in the Red Bull this weekend.

In a recent development, most of the teams waited and waited to come out and then suddenly lots of drivers are sent out, resulting in a queue in the pits! With the high track temperatures and high degradation, the drivers are crawling around on their out laps to preserve these soft tyres.

In a recent development, bumper to bumper in the pit lane! #F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/ff8JO9kB1g.

The two Haas drivers have a free track to themselves whilst everyone else bides their time. In theory, as the hour of qualifying goes on, the track temperature should decrease and the more rubber that is laid down the faster the track should get.

Finally, just before the two Haas drivers finish their first flying laps, the rest of the grid is starting to emerge, led by the Mercedes duo.

The green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and Q1 is officially under way. The two Haas drivers are the first to head out. Other than that, it is a quiet start to Q1.

Recent findings suggest that the top four teams; Mercedes, Red Bull, Ferrari and McLaren, all have a genuine chance of taking pole in Sepang today. I think the true favourites though have to be the Mercedes duo and Max Verstappen but with how close it between all four of the teams you cannot rule anything out.

It is 33 degrees celsius air temperature, with the track temperature up at 58 degrees.

Not long to wait now until qualifying begins. It is hot, humid and dry in Sepang right now. As we know in Malaysia, the weather can change swiftly and thunderstorms can roll in quite quickly but it looks like today’s qualifying will be a dry one. This will be one of if not the hottest qualifying sessions of the season, so much so that we are seeing umbrellas going up to get some shade from the sun rather than sheltering from any rain.

This will be crucial to consider after qualifying finishes as there will be some shuffling around:.

Isack Hadjar (Red Bull): five-place grid penalty- upcoming internal combustion engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): ten-place grid penalty- new engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): five-place grid penalty- causing a collision in BakuArvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls): back of the grid- complete power unit change.

In a recent development, hadjar has looked good since returning from his wrist injury so could be fighting it out near the front of the grid, although his five-place penalty will drop him down. We know Lindblad will be at the back and is very likely to be joined there by Colapinto, who is not going to be qualifying high up in the top ten in his Alpine.

Haas have announced that Frenchman Esteban Ocon will leave at the end of this season. Ocon now faces an uncertain future, with it difficult to see a spot for him on the F1 grid next season. There are suggestions that the 30-year-old’s replacement will be Brazilian Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, although nothing has been confirmed on that front. 21-year-old Camara at the moment leads the Formula 2 championship.

TGR Haas F1 Team and Esteban Ocon will part ways at the conclusion of the 2026 season. With plenty of racing ahead, our focus remains on working together to maximize every opportunity through to the final race of the year.#HaasF1 #F1 pic.twitter.com/4iQAuqnSyA.

It has been revealed that aston Martin have now confirmed their driver line-up for next season, retaining both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll. There had been reports that Alonso had been contemplating retirement but the 45-year-old will continue into another season.

Sources indicate that aston Martin Aramco confirms Lance and Fernando will continue as the team's drivers in 2027. Read more: ​https://t.co/ePyjJdyAIB pic.twitter.com/VogFUEbNxy.

Other than the second seat alongside Ollie Bearman at Haas, the only other team to keep an eye on is Racing Bulls, with no definite confirmation on their exact driver line-up for next season.

Ferrari this week have publicly backed their team principal Frederic Vasseur, amid speculation over the Frenchman’s position and comments made by former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner, who said the job at Ferrari would be a “dream job”. Ferrari, who sit second in the constructors’ standings, have not won the drivers’ championship since 2007 (Kimi Raikkonen) and the constructors’ since 2008. Here is a snippet from Tom Cary’s piece on the matter:.

In a hastily convened media call on Tuesday morning, Maria Conti, Ferrari’s chief communication officer, said the Scuderia had decided to issue a vote of confidence in Vasseur in response “not just to the story of Mr Horner, but in general, the speculation about Fred”.

“Ferrari has made its choices,” Conti said. “We have confidence – full confidence – in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so.

“At this time, it’s really notable that the team remains united and cohesive, and we are focused with all the energy on the work ahead.”.

Recent findings suggest that “It is great to be back [in Malaysia]. I am really enjoying the track. We have had some wonderful races here over time. It is actually the 20th time we have been here, it started in 1999, and it is really exciting to be back. I really enjoyed getting out on the track and watching the cars closely.

It has been revealed that “The drivers are super fit and they have some cooling but it is not easy. But you almost cannot get enough fluid through your body before your stomach gives up. Having this race and Singapore back-to-back increases that challenge.”.

Especially with the significant upgrade they have brought this weekend, Mercedes’ lead at the summit is looking unassailable right now.

Almost nine years ago to the day, Max Verstappen took just his second race victory in Formula 1. Lewis Hamilton, who took pole position, and Daniel Ricciardo joined Verstappen on the podium. Despite being nine years ago, plenty of drivers still on the grid were racing that weekend. Here they are and who they were racing for:.

Max Verstappen (Red Bull) Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes) Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes) Esteban Ocon (Force India)Nico Hulkenberg (Renault)Sergio Perez (Force India)Fernando Alonso (McLaren)Lance Stroll (Williams)Carlos Sainz (Toro Rosso)Pierre Gasly (Toro Rosso).

With Russell winning in Baku and Antonelli finishing fifth, the latter’s championship lead was cut to 66 points. If Russell is going to usurp his teammate, he is going to need a few more similar results to last weekend due to the size of Antonelli’s lead. If Antonelli were to suffer a retirement, then that completely changes the outlook.

Formula One returns to Malaysia for round 16 of the season for the Bahrain Grand Prix. That probably sounds strange but after the Bahrain Grand Prix was originally postponed in March, F1 reinstated it to the calendar with Malaysia hosting it because of the ongoing war in the Middle East. Despite being held in Malaysia, Bahrain have retained the naming rights for the event, which is officially known as the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The last time Formula One was in Malaysia was nine years ago back in 2017, when a young whippersnapper named Max Verstappen, still four years away from winning his first world championship, claimed just his second victory.

According to recent reports, last time out around the streets of Baku, Mercedes’ George Russell claimed victory at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, pipping Verstappen by just a tenth of a second. That was Russell’s first grand prix win since June and cuts his team-mate Kimi Antonelli’s lead in the drivers’ standings to 66 points. Antonelli had a challenging weekend in Baku, starting 16th after a crash in qualifying and coming home in fifth to see his championship lead to Russell cut by 15 points.

According to recent reports, verstappen was quickest in first practice yesterday, with the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc fastest in second practice. Earlier today, championship leader Antonelli was nearly three tenths clear of the field in third practice. Mercedes, 160 points clear at the top of the constructors’ standings, have brought significant upgrades this weekend, which includes a fresh floor, rear suspension and rear corner. It is the team’s first significant car upgrade since the Canadian Grand at the end of May.

This race in Malaysia represents the second leg of the season’s first flyaway triple header, with the Singapore Grand Prix to come next weekend, so the demands on the teams and the drivers are incredibly high. Qualifying from Sepang gets under way at 9am (GMT).

A very positive record: Luca Pairetto will officiate Milan’s game against Frosinone

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Luca Pairetto has been assigned to the game between AC Milan and Frosinone on Sunday evening, which is good news for the Rossoneri.

According to recent reports, ruben Amorim and his men will be looking to make it three consecutive wins against Frosinone, after beating Inter and Genoa before the international break. It might not be such an easy task, though, as admitted by the gaffer himself in his press conference.

In a recent development, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Frosinone have indeed started the season well, at the moment sitting in sixth place, and they don’t really have anything to lose from their trip to San Siro. Only something to gain, which can always make things tricky for the favourite.

In a recent development, given the above, as always, Milan will be hoping for good officiating to keep the away side from disrupting the play too much. The Italian Referees Association, also known as AIA, unveiled the referees for this weekend’s game a few days ago and for the Rossoneri, it will be Luca Pairetto.

The 42-year-old is definitely one of the more experienced referees around, even if he has never reached the heights of some of his colleagues. In any case, he has officiated 12 games involving Milan so far and the record is positive: 9 wins, 2 draws and 1 defeat.

Industry observers note that it’s been a while since he last officiated a Milan game, though, as we have to go back to the 2024-25 season. The Rossoneri played Empoli and beat them 2-0, courtesy of goals from Rafael Leao and Santiago Gimenez.

Despite the win, the game wasn’t without controversy. A red card was not given to Empoli despite a reckless challenge, and Fikayo Tomori was then given a second yellow when the whole sequence should have been stopped due to offside.

However, most of those errors were made by VAR or the assistant referee and not Pairetto himself.

Blackpool will be looking to end their poor form when they welcome Leicester City to Bloomfield Road on Tuesday evening.

The hosts currently sit 22nd in the League One table, while the visitors are 10th.

Blackpool are in the relegation zone after making a poor start to the season that ultimately cost Ian Evatt his job, with the head coach sacked on his birthday following a run of three league games without a win.

In their first game under caretaker boss Steve Thompson, Blackpool were beaten 2-1 by Wigan Athletic despite taking the lead through Zac Ashworth.

Thompson branded the result "frustrating" and "disappointing" and they will be keen to bounce back on Tuesday.

However, it is worth noting that Blackpool have not beaten Leicester in their last eight meetings across all competitions.

Leicester, meanwhile, look to have found some form in recent weeks after a disappointing start to the season under Russell Martin.

The Foxes picked up just two wins in their first eight league matches, but have since won four of their next six to leave them just one point outside the playoffs.

Leicester beat Huddersfield 1-0 at the weekend thanks to teenager Louis Page, who scored his first league goal for the club, and they will be full of confidence heading into Tuesday's clash.

The Huddersfield victory was particularly impressive as the Terriers were top ahead of the fixture and had only suffered one league defeat.

Leicester City League One form:.

Leicester City form (all competitions):.

Blackpool have a number of injury problems and had only one fit centre-back for Saturday's defeat against Wigan in Oliver Casey.

Dale Taylor was also forced off with an injury on Saturday and is expected to be replaced by Leighton Clarkson for Tuesday's game.

Leicester will have to make at least one change after Will Smallbone picked up an injury against Huddersfield, with Page set to replace him.

Emil Riis is expected to lead the line, with support from Sammy Braybrooke and Kamari Doyle.

Blackpool possible starting lineup:.

Peacock-Farrell; Williams, Casey, Ashworth; Bowler, Brown, Morgan, Hamilton; Taylor; Charles, Yates.

Leicester City possible starting lineup:.

McCarthy; Souttar, O'Hora, Okoli; Alves, Lundstram, Page, Thomas; Doyle, Braybrooke; Riis.

Leicester will be flying high after an important win at the weekend and should have enough to beat managerless Blackpool.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that hundreds of millions of people around the world are affected by diabetes mellitus1. It develops when the activity of insulin, a glucose-lowering hormone secreted by pancreatic β-cells, becomes insufficient to maintain healthy glucose levels in the blood. The condition can be managed with oral medication or by injecting insulin and other metabolic hormones, but the constant need for people with diabetes to manage their lifestyle and blood-glucose levels can impair their quality of life. Therapeutic approaches that monitor and control blood glucose automatically are therefore highly desirable. Writing in Nature, Xiu et al.2 report proof of principle of a bioelectronic device called NeuroAxis that does exactly that in rat models of diabetes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matthew Cooper | 22 Nov 2026 15:14, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 15:14.

Bromley will be looking to pick up another victory when they welcome Wycombe Wanderers to the CopperJax Community Stadium on Tuesday evening.

The hosts currently sit 23rd in the League One table, while the visitors are 15th.

Bromley finally ended their woeful run of form on Saturday, securing a hugely important 1-0 victory away to promotion contenders Reading.

Victor Adeboyejo scored the only goal of the game and goalkeeper Shamal George made a host of impressive save to help the Ravens claim all three points.

That win ended a run of 10 games without a victory across all competitions and was Karl Robinson's first since he replaced Andy Woodman as head coach earlier this month.

It also saw Bromley move off the foot of the table, leaving them just one point from safety.

However, they do have the worst defensive record in the division, having conceded 33 goals in 14 games so far.

Wycombe, meanwhile, will be looking to bounce back from a disappointing defeat to Oxford United on Saturday.

The Chairboys suffered a remarkable 4-3 loss despite the fact they were 3-0 ahead going into the final 20 minutes.

Goals from Jayden Wareham, Malik Mothersille and Aaron Morley had put Wycombe in a commanding position, but Oxford scored four late goals to pick up a stunning victory.

Tom Hounsell's side also ended the game with nine men after Dan Casey and Luke Leahy were sent off.

Hounsell admitted the defeat was a "bitter pill to swallow", but felt his side "dominated the game" for 70 minutes and must take heart from that.

Bromley form (all competitions):.

Wycombe Wanderers form (all competitions):.

Bromley could hand Adeboyejo a start after he scored off the bench against Reading, with Michael Cheek set to drop to the bench.

Jodi Jones and Mickel Miller could continue out wide, with Kamil Conteh and George Saville set to start in midfield.

Wycombe will be without Casey and Leahy, with the pair suspended following their red cards against Oxford.

Steve Cook is set to replace Casey in defence, while Wareham is expected to continue up front.

Bromley possible starting lineup:.

George; Ifill, Oxford, Taylor, Mendy; Jones, Conteh, Saville, Miller; Adeboyejo, Pinnock.

Wycombe Wanderers possible starting lineup:.

Hazard; Grimmer, Cook, Taylor, Hagelskjaer; Morley, Scowen; Thomas, Boyd-Munce, Mothersille; Wareham.

Bromley will be full of confidence after beating Reading and we are backing them to pick up a point against a Wycombe side that capitulated in dramatic fashion against Oxford.

GdS: Possession vs. directness – key tactical differences between Milan and Frosinone

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (515 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sempremilan

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ruben Amorim will be up against Massimiliano Alvini tomorrow evening, and as the stats show, they are two very different managers.
  • As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport, there is one interesting stat to highlight to introduce the game.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ruben Amorim will be up against Massimiliano Alvini tomorrow evening, and as the stats show, they are two very different managers.

As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport, there is one interesting stat to highlight to introduce the game. In terms of shots per game, it will be the second-ranked team and against the 17th-ranked team. That in itself won’t raise any eyebrows, but the fact that Milan are the ones in 17th place will.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Recent findings suggest that the Rossoneri have mustered a mere 126 shots so far, while Frosinone are quite far ahead at 221. On the flip side, the newly-promoted side have only scored one more goal than Milan (24 vs. 23), which is what makes this game so interesting.

According to recent reports, amorim has made it clear from the start that he wants to dominate each game. That indicates in the possession, as Milan are third in Serie A with an average of 59% so far, and they also rank high in terms of passes per game.

In a recent development, the shots are where they fall short, even if they average over two goals per game. There are several reasons for this, but most of it can be attributed to Amorim’s recent arrival and the fact that he has experimented rather extensively.

During today’s presser, he even said that they haven’t done anywhere near enough to enter the penalty box more often, which tends to mean more shots.

In the build-up, for example, the Rossoneri move the ball forward at an average speed of 1.30 meters per second, which is the slowest in Serie A. Alvini’s Frosinone, on the other hand, are great at vertical football: the ball moves toward the opponent’s penalty box at 2.51 meters per second, the best rate in the league.

Recent findings suggest that the Ciociari are masters of rapid counterattacks, so much so that on only 40 occasions have they built plays with ten or more passes. Milan, meanwhile, have 203.

Sources indicate that everything starts in the defence phase for Frosinone. Indeed, they always attempt to win the ball back inside the opponent’s half, which is proven by the index that measures the intensity of pressing in the attacking zone (they are first in Serie A).

Milan? They are eighth, despite being – along with Como – the team to have scored the most goals (4) from a ball recovered while pressing.

The difference between the two is well explained by the so-called “pressed sequences”, that is, the number of actions in open play in which a team manages to interrupt the opponent’s build-up within three passes or less, before the ball goes beyond the halfway line.

It has been revealed that on that front, Frosinone are also first (161), while Milan are only 15th (102). Having stated all of this, as the pink newspaper concludes, we should expect a spectacular match tomorrow. Both teams will stick to their respective game, which bodes well.

The next Lamine Yamal? Why not? Roberto De Zerbi sets high bar for Luca Williams-Barnett after 18-year-old thrilled Tottenham fans in win over Ipswich, writes MATT BARLOW

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (803 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 06:34 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • Luca Williams-Barnett will score better goals.
  • Roberto De Zerbi compared him to Lamine Yamal after watching the 18-year-old steal the show as Spurs beat Ipswich, their fourth win in five to move within three points of the top four.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 06:34 EST, 22 November 2026.

Luca Williams-Barnett will score better goals. That was the consensus on a day when the Tottenham starlet marked his first Premier League by scoring the first and creating the second.

Roberto De Zerbi compared him to Lamine Yamal after watching the 18-year-old steal the show as Spurs beat Ipswich, their fourth win in five to move within three points of the top four.

Industry observers note that 'He is a special player, I am not surprised,' stated De Zerbi. 'I decided 10 days ago he would play and I asked him two things. First, to play like he is on the park with his friends and then to work hard without the ball, like Raphinha and Yamal.

'In football today players with talent have to work hard and attackers are the first defenders.'.

Sources indicate that asked if Williams-Barnett could aspire to the levels of Barcelona’s Yamal, the Spurs boss replied: 'Yes, I think so'. And told how on the teenager had spent the bus ride to the stadium watching clips of Ronaldinho, Neymar and Eden Hazard on YouTube.

His goal was a picture of youthful desire and determination to get across his marker at the back post and be first to a delicious teasing cross delivered by Pedro Porro.

Roberto De Zerbi rates Williams-Barnett as ‘one of the best’ young players he has worked with.

Williams-Barnett slid and stretched past Abdoul Ouattara with his right foot as the ball skipped and hit him high on the left thigh before rebounding into the bottom corner.

Recent findings suggest that you make your own luck. The Spurs crowd erupted. They have been waiting to hail another of their own. Maybe this is the one. A goal on his first start, just like Harry Kane, and at 18 years and 51 days, the club’s youngest league scorer since Gareth Bale.

Industry observers note that there has been a buzz growing around Williams-Barnett for the last 18 months as he rose through the academy ranks. He made his England Under-19 debut in September, coming on as a sub for Max Dowman, Arsenal’s teenage sensation.

De Zerbi adores his attitude as much as his talent, and a confidence bordering arrogance on display in pre-season when he dinked in a ‘Panenka’ style penalty in a shootout in Australia.

He is right-footed but started against Ipswich wide on the left, in the role no player has made their own since Heung-min Son.

Dominic Solanke, who scored Tottenham's second goal, congratulates his young team-mate.

Williams-Barnett might have had a second before half time, a half-chance miscued and a header saved.

According to recent reports, spurs fans responded. When he picked up the ball on halfway early in the second half, they roared him forward into the space ahead. He duly obliged, through the gears into a swagger and into the Ipswich penalty box without meeting a challenge.

Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Kinsky 6; Porro 7, Van Hecke 6, Senesi 6, Udogie 6 (Robertson 80); Fernandes 7, Gallagher 7; Kudus 6, Maddison 7 (Bergvall 64, 5), Williams-Barnett 8 (Savio 64, 6 (Gray 90)); Solanke 7 (Marmoush 64, 5).

Scorers: Williams-Barnett, Solanke.

Booked: Maddison, Williams-Barnett, Kudus, Fernandes.

Ipswich (3-4-2-1): Walton 7; Furlong 5, Diop 5, O’Shea 6; Outtara 4 (Fatawu 56, 5), Palacios 5 (Florentino 56, 5), Lukic 6, Davis 6 (Greaves 82); Enciso 5, Maeda 5 (Clarke 56, 5); Flemming 6.

Sources indicate that belatedly, Darnell Furlong tried to hold him up. But Williams-Barnett made a yard on the outside and whipped over a cross with his left foot, which fizzed past Walton and was turned in from close range by Dominic Solanke.

The teenager booted the ball jubilantly into the crowd and collected his first yellow card from killjoy referee Rob Jones.

In a recent development, williams-Barnett left to a standing ovation when he was replaced by Savio in the 64th minute. 'Luca was magnificent,' noted Solanke. 'To see him do that on his first Premier League start is crazy.'.

Sources indicate that spurs coasted in. It had been comfortable, even without some senior players including Sandro Tonali who had been unwell.

They were solid at the back and creative up front, peppering the Ipswich goal with 18 shots. Mohamed Kudus struck a post from a first-half free kick, won by Williams-Barnett.

Christian Walton made strong saves to deny James Maddison and prevent Dara O’Shea turning into his own goal.

It has been revealed that savio cross hit a post with a deflected cross before he was struck down by a recurrence of the hamstring injury which ruled him out for six weeks. It was the only blemish for De Zerbi, although one to enhance the opportunities ahead for Williams-Barnett.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 22 Nov 2026 15:18, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 15:25.

Liverpool and Manchester United have confirmed their starting lineups for Sunday's Premier League clash at Anfield.

In his first game as Red Devils head coach, Mauricio Pochettino has made three changes to the starting lineup from Michael Carrick's last outing - the chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa before the international break.

Two of those changes come in defence, where the Argentine has unexpectedly recalled Matthijs de Ligt, for what will be the Dutchman's first Premier League start in nearly a year.

De Ligt has not made a Premier League XI since November 30, 2025, but the 27-year-old is preferred to Harry Maguire alongside Lisandro Martinez in central defence.

Martinez - back from suspension - is also restored to the starting lineup in place of Noussair Mazraoui, meaning that Leny Yoro will move across to right-back, and Diogo Dalot continues on the left with Luke Shaw still injured.

Pochettino's third and final alteration sees Patrick Dorgu replace Amad Diallo in the final third, where Matheus Cunha is expected to operate through the middle as Bryan Mbeumo bombs down the right.

It has been revealed that ? Presenting today's starting XI, in positional order... https://t.co/pFYEqexFSk.

As for Liverpool, Iraola has made just one change to the team that started the 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park two weekends ago.

The hosting manager has seemingly been forced into that alteration, as Rio Ngumoha comes in for Cody Gakpo, who is absent from the squad entirely.

Concern was raised over Gakpo's fitness when the attacker was not seen arriving at the team hotel, and Iraola will likely explain his absence when he faces the media before kickoff.

Elsewhere, Ryan Gravenberch has not yet recovered from a heel injury, so Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister continue as the double pivot with Trey Nyoni in reserve.

Jeremie Frimpong is back on the bench following a hamstring problem, but Ronald Araujo is unsurprisingly retained at right-back in an unchanged Liverpool defence.

A draw or win for Man United will lift them out of the relegation zone in the Premier League table, while Liverpool will leapfrog Bournemouth into fourth place if they avoid defeat.

Liverpool XI: Alisson; Araujo, Van Dijk, Jacquet, Kerkez; Szoboszlai, Mac Allister; Ngumoha, Wirtz, Barcola; Isak.

Subs: Mamardashvili, Gomez, Chiesa, Tsimikas, Munoz, Frimpong, Nyoni, McConnell, Koumas.

Man United XI: Lammens; Yoro, De Ligt, Martinez, Dalot; Tielemans, Mainoo; Mbeumo, Fernandes, Dorgu; Cunha.

Subs: Heaton, Heaven, Maguire, Mazraoui, Santos, Mount, Amad, Lacey, Zirkzee.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As he left Milanello earlier this evening, Gerry Cardinale stopped to share a few words on the game against Frosinone, the January mercato, Markus Krösche and more.

Cardinale arrived in Milan a few days ago and had a summit with the management at Casa Milan yesterday. In other words, he’s not wasting any time, making every second of his trip to the city count.

Sources indicate that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Today, he was at Milanello to watch the team’s training session and Amorim’s press conference, and tomorrow he will be at the game against Frosinone.

The owner left the training ground shortly after 4 pm today, but before driving away, he rolled down the window and spoke to the journalists present. In addition to the game, he also spoke about the upcoming mercato and what Milan intend to do.

“I’m ready for tomorrow. We had a great couple of days, including a session at Casa Milan yesterday on the mercato, as well as the rest of our plans for the season going into the summer. I’d say that the mood is really upbeat here, it was a great session today and the team is really coming together.

It has been revealed that “I spoke to a bunch of the players, they are all feeling really positive, and they understand as Ruben said how important tomorrow’s game is. Hopefully, we come out strong, get the win and keep going.”.

According to recent reports, “Yeah I’m ready. We are doing a lot of work. It’s complicated and the January transfer window is always tricky. So you have to be prepared, you have to be opportunistic. The one thing I can promise is that we won’t make any decision that we don’t feel great about.

“We will spend money, but we will spend money smart and with a view to being consistent with the project, in close coordination with Ruben and everyone here at Milanello.”.

“With Markus Krösche. I know you guys have been very focused on Markus, but when we’re ready to make an announcement, I will come back to you guys on it.”.

In a recent development, “Look, that name also keeps getting mentioned. This project is more than just one player, but he’s one of the best players, if not the best player, in his position. So tremendous amount of respect from me and we will see what’s possible.”.

Industry observers note that “Look, I love Adrien, he’s one of my favourite players. I think he’s just fantastic and I have a tremendous amount of respect for him and his family. We are in discussions and I hope that we will have a good result. But if it were up to me, he would be a franchise player.”.

Clearly, there’s a lot happening right now and Milan are hoping that the addition of Krösche to the management will help them get even better control. It would certainly raise the enthusiasm if they were to have a good mercato and secure a renewal for Adrien Rabiot.

Sources indicate that cardinale: “Ho parlato con i giocatori sono molto concentrati. Endrick e’ uno dei migliori giocatori al mondo, ci proveremo, vediamo se sarà una possibilità di mercato. Rabiot? E’ un giocatore fantastico vogliamo che sia anche per il futuro” https://t.co/bf9mcZulbG.

#152457. Liverpool vs. Man Utd:. Andoni Iraola explains Cody Gakpo, Ryan Gravenberch absences

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Liverpool vs. Man Utd:. Andoni Iraola explains Cody Gakpo, Ryan Gravenberch absences

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (483 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Knapton | 22 Nov 2026 16:02, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 16:14.
  • Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has explained why Cody Gakpo and Ryan Gravenberch are missing from the squad to face Manchester United in Sunday's Premier League clash.
  • Neither Dutchman was included in the Liverpool starting lineup or bench for the visit of the Red Devils, after also not being seen arriving at the team hotel on Sunday morning.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 22 Nov 2026 16:02, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 16:14.

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has explained why Cody Gakpo and Ryan Gravenberch are missing from the squad to face Manchester United in Sunday's Premier League clash.

Neither Dutchman was included in the Liverpool starting lineup or bench for the visit of the Red Devils, after also not being seen arriving at the team hotel on Sunday morning.

Gravenberch was already known to be carrying a heel injury, but Gakpo's absence came as a surprise, as the attacker was not name-checked in Iraola's pre-game fitness upgrade.

However, speaking to Sky Sports ahead of kickoff, the Liverpool boss revealed that Gakpo picked up a calf injury during the international break and is yet to return to team training.

Industry observers note that "Gakpo got injured with the Netherlands, he left the game with a soleus injury," Iraola stated. “He hasn’t been training with us, nothing since getting injured from the national team.".

Regarding Gravenberch, Iraola did not rule out a comeback for the midfielder against Club Brugge in Wednesday's Champions League clash, adding: "Ryan has been training but still is managing the pain.

According to recent reports, “With Ryan we are going day to day – some days he can. We have been waiting until the end but he was in pain yesterday. Let’s hope we can recover him for the next one.".

Gakpo's absence is particularly damaging for both the Dutchman and Liverpool, as he has scored more Premier League goals against Man United than any other team.

Indeed, Gakpo boasts five goals from seven previous top-flight games against the Red Devils, scoring in each of his last three Premier League outings against the 20-time English champions.

Only against West Ham United (7) has Gakpo scored more goals against across all competitions, four in the Premier League and three in the EFL Cup.

Iraola did not disclose the severity of Gakpo's calf injury, which could be grouped into one of three categories; a Grade 1 mild strain, a Grade 2 mild tear, or a Grade 3 complete rupture.

If Gakpo has got away with the least serious calf problem, the Dutchman should only miss a maximum of two weeks, and he could potentially return in time for the Merseyside derby next weekend.

However, Gakpo is expected to sit out Wednesday's Champions League clash with Club Brugge, and a Grade 2 injury could sideline the former PSV Eindhoven man for the rest of the calendar year.

A Grade 3 tear would likely rule Gakpo out for around three months, putting him at risk of missing games against Inter Milan, Man United, Arsenal and Everton between now and February 6.

James Pearce reports that Gakpo has avoided a serious problem, though either Ngumoha or Victor Munoz should be given the nod from the first whistle against Club Brugge.

Christy Grimshaw was crucial as AC Milan Women finally got back to winning ways, following what was a rather crazy first half against Sassuolo.

After two defeats and a draw, dropping points in a silly fashion against Napoli last weekend, Milan Women needed to bounce back with a win today. Thankfully, that’s exactly what they managed to do, even if it wasn’t the most controlled performance.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Just looking at the scoreline and the timing of the goals is enough to understand the nature of the game. All five goals were scored in the first half and it doesn’t end there either. All five were scored within the first 27 minutes!

According to recent reports, the veteran Grimshaw opened the scoring for the Rossonere after nine minutes, but Sassuolo found a way back into the game just two minutes later. The Scottish international decided to restore the lead just four minutes later, i.e. in the 15th minute.

It has been revealed that angelica Soffia then made things more comfortable with a third goal in the 24th minute, or at least so we thought. Just three minutes after that, Sassuolo scored again and thus brought some life into the game, even if Milan looked the better side.

Recent findings suggest that suzanne Bakker’s side actually dominated possession, had more shots on target and also had a higher xG, so the win definitely feels deserved. And boy was it needed! The situation in the standings is still not great, but at least they are now four points behind the Champions League zone.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Nolan | 22 Nov 2026 16:20, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 20:57.
  • Manchester City will look to climb the Champions League table and restart their season by beating visitors Napoli at the Etihad on Tuesday.
  • The Citizens are seventh with nine points in the league phase and right now occupy one of eight automatic spots for the round of 16, whereas their Italian opponents are 27th with just three points after four gamedays.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 22 Nov 2026 16:20, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 20:57.

Manchester City will look to climb the Champions League table and restart their season by beating visitors Napoli at the Etihad on Tuesday.

The Citizens are seventh with nine points in the league phase and right now occupy one of eight automatic spots for the round of 16, whereas their Italian opponents are 27th with just three points after four gamedays.

City's woes in the Premier League continued on Saturday afternoon, when they were held to a 1-1 stalemate by Fulham, who left their hosts third in the Premier League table.

Enzo Maresca's side have now lost three and drawn one of their past four top-flight outings, while they have won four and lost four of their nine most recent matches.

One of those defeats was a 4-2 loss against Paris Saint-Germain on October 24 in their fourth Champions League clash of the season.

The hosts' defensive frailties were routinely exposed by PSG, and it should concern fans the club have conceded at least two goals in seven of their last 11 fixtures, a period in which they kept just one clean sheet.

Maresca's side have still largely succeeded at home considering they have triumphed in seven of their 10 contests at the Etihad this term, suffering two defeats in that time.

City have conceded 14 goals in their past seven clashes at the stadium, while they managed to find the back of the net on 18 occasions.

Kevin De Bruyne will return to the Etihad once again as a Napoli player, though his side have been defeated in each of their last three meetings with their English hosts.

The visitors appointed Massimiliano Allegri as the successor to Antonio Conte, who won Serie A in 2024-25, the Supercoppa Italiana in 2025-26 and guided the club to second place in May, but the current manager's spell in the dugout has been disastrous.

The visitors have won six of their 16 fixtures this campaign, and they head to the Etihad having been beaten in two of their past four games, emerging as victors once.

Gli Azzurri are eighth in the Serie A table with 18 points following their 1-0 win against Torino on Saturday, and their situation in Europe is also concerning given they have lost to Arsenal, Villarreal and Porto.

They have conceded 11 times so far in the Champions League, and though they have netted six goals, they scored just six goals in their past seven away contests in all competitions.

Napoli were beaten in five of those seven matches on the road, with their only victory a 4-1 win against Monza on October 28.

Manchester City Champions League form:.

Manchester City form (all competitions):.

Napoli form (all competitions):.

Man City know they will be without winger Antoine Semenyo, while there are also concerns about right-back Matheus Nunes.

Should both miss out, expect to see Abdukodir Khusanov on the right side of defence, with Iliman Ndiaye and Jeremy Doku on the flanks.

Midfielder Enzo Fernandez was left out of the XI against Fulham, but he will likely return in place of teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Napoli will be without defender Giovanni Di Lorenzo and the banned Rafa Marin, so perhaps Amir Rrahmani and Sam Beukema will line up in a two-man central defensive pairing.

With midfielder Stanislav Lobotka ruled out, it would not be surprising to see Frank Anguissa, Billy Gilmour and Scott McTominay stationed in the middle of the pitch.

De Bruyne could be used in an advanced role in order to alleviate him of defensive responsibilities, though he will be expected to supply striker Rasmus Hojlund.

Manchester City possible starting lineup:.

Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Guehi, Gvardiol; Anderson, Fernandez; Ndiaye, Cherki, Doku; Haaland.

Napoli possible starting lineup:.

Milinkovic-Savic; Politano, Rrahmani, Beukema, Spinazzola; Anguissa, Gilmour, McTominay; De Bruyne; Hojlund, Lang.

Regardless of City's poor form, it is difficult to see Napoli travelling to the Etihad and defying their record against the Citizens to claim three points.

However, the hosts have been far too open defensively, and the club's frailties at the back could lead to yet another disappointing result.

Breaking: O'Neill hails recalled midfield duo Oxlade-Chamberlain and McCowan after both net to help sink St Mirren

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:17 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 15:31 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Celtic manager Martin O’Neill hailed midfield duo Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan after the recalled pair both scored in the 4-1 home win over St Mirren.
  • With Mika Baur facing 10 weeks out with an ankle injury and Benjamin Nygren nursing a heel problem, O’Neill handed McCowan his second start of the season and Oxlade-Chamberlain his fifth, as the two joined forces for the first time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 15:17 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 15:31 EST, 21 November 2026.

Celtic manager Martin O’Neill hailed midfield duo Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan after the recalled pair both scored in the 4-1 home win over St Mirren.

With Mika Baur facing 10 weeks out with an ankle injury and Benjamin Nygren nursing a heel problem, O’Neill handed McCowan his second start of the season and Oxlade-Chamberlain his fifth, as the two joined forces for the first time.

Oxlade-Chamberlain and McCowan netted either side of Camilo Duran in a nine-minute flurry of goals late in the first half with Callum McGregor making it four for Celtic in the second period before Killian Phillips reduced the deficit for Saints from the penalty spot.

It has been revealed that O’Neill remarked: ‘Alex has been waiting around for a while to get into the side. He’s a brilliant passer of the ball. He took his goal very well with a calm finish in the bottom corner.

‘He was feeling a little bit sore, so taking him off was just precautionary.

‘I was also delighted Luke got his goal. That should give him a boost in confidence.’.

Oxlade-Chamberlain congratulates McCowan after he scored to make it three for Celtic.

McCowan faced criticism after Celtic’s Champions League collapse against LASK and his only previous start this season saw him taken off at half-time in a home defeat by Rangers.

O’Neill said: ‘I thought he did really well, also playing the full game given it has been some considerable time since he has done that.

‘He got the ball early on and played it almost blindly and it was intercepted and I thought, “oh, gosh, here we go”. But he roared back, took his goal well and I am really pleased for him. He is a real genuine lad.

It has been revealed that ‘It has been tough for him. In the game against Rangers, he was thrown into a position, and it didn’t start well for him in the match. I think he felt it was deja vu for him in terms of the game at the back end of last season too. That will be good for him.’.

The Celtic manager also introduced 19-year-old former PSV Eindhoven midfielder Joel van den Berg for a debut in the second half.

In a recent development, ‘I thought he did very well,’ noted O’Neill. ‘He’s coming on after an injury which kept him out for some time.

‘I am pleased there is a bit of competition for places now.’.

The veteran midfielder celebrates his strike that opened the scoring against St Mirren.

St Mirren manager Craig McLeish felt Celtic were clinical in his team’s heavy defeat in Glasgow.

‘It’s a really sore one with the way the scoreline ended up,’ said McLeish.

It has been revealed that ‘I thought we started the game quite well and then that flurry of goals can happen here when you’re playing against such a strong team. The difference was the quality in our box compared to theirs.

‘They are just so clinical, and they get into those good areas and they punish you.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I felt we got into some similar areas throughout the game. We didn’t give up, we didn’t move away from what we were trying to do, but we were just really lacking that final bit.’.
